title: GTM (DACH)
descriptionHtml:
We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role

We are looking for an enthusiastic, driven, and proactive commercial analyst to join our expanding DACH go-to-market team. As a key member of our commercial team, you will play a crucial role in sourcing and qualifying leads, initiating outreach, and scheduling high-value conversations for our Account Executives. Your goal will be to create meaningful connections with healthcare practices and hospital groups, facilitating our mission to win across the DACH market.

This role requires a proactive mindset, excellent communication skills, and the ability to thrive in a high-growth startup environment. You will become an expert in engaging healthcare stakeholders, driving new opportunities, and contributing directly to the sales pipeline.

What you’ll do

  • Identify, research, and prospect potential customers and formulate go-to-market strategies

  • Execute inbound and outbound campaigns using a mix of calls, emails, social selling, and product-led signals to qualify leads.

  • Schedule high-quality meetings and product demonstrations for Account Executives, ensuring smooth handoff of qualified opportunities.

  • Own and manage end-to-end sales cycles for small SMB customers, from initial outreach through to closing deals.

  • Maintain accurate records in HubSpot CRM, manage and optimise sales pipelines, and consistently meet targets for qualified leads generated.

  • Collaborate closely with Account Executives, Marketing, Product, Operations, and Customer Success teams to streamline sales strategies and market positioning.

  • Stay updated on market trends, competitor activities, and evolving customer needs to identify new opportunities.

What we're looking for

  • 1-2 years of experience in sales or in tech, banking, consulting, PE/VC or similar.

  • Proven success in generating leads, qualifying prospects, and managing high-volume outreach campaigns.

  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, able to quickly build rapport and articulate the value of Heidi’s AI-driven healthcare solutions.

  • Highly organised, disciplined, and results-oriented with a strong problem-solving ability and the ability to prioritise multiple tasks simultaneously.

  • Comfortable working independently in a dynamic, fast-paced startup environment with a high degree of accountability.

  • Eager to learn, adaptable, and excited about professional growth opportunities.

Attitude is more important than experience so if you are a hungry, competitive and highly motivated operator who has a knack for problem solving and building relationships we want to hear from you.

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

We take care of you.

We chose to open-source our benefits hub, if you care to take a peek.

title: Head of Applied AI
descriptionHtml:
Head of Applied AI

Location: Our offices are in Central London, along with several of our customers. Travel to our customer sites is required, the frequency of which will vary from customer-to-customer. You need to be able to travel onsite to London up to 3 days per week, although onsite requirements will vary week-to-week and customer-to-customer from 0 to 3 days.

Defence/SC Clearance Requirements:

SC clearance is required for our customer facing teams. You do not need active SC clearance as we will undertake checks upon you joining, but you must be eligible to pass SC clearance. DV clearance may be required for certain roles, so the ability/willingness to pass DV clearance is advantageous but not essential.

About Cloudscaler

Cloudscaler is a rapidly growing cloud consultancy. We partner with ambitious enterprise and public sector customers to design, build, operate, and support secure, governed cloud platforms that meet the highest regulatory and industry standards.

We are scaling deliberately. Our revenue ambition depends on deploying the right people onto the right work quickly, and on making disciplined use of our capacity. This role is central to that.

 

About the role

Cloudscaler's Applied AI business unit launched at the start of 2026 and has grown quickly, with an established offering, live client engagements and a pipeline in place. The current Head of Applied AI is stepping back from the role for personal reasons and remains with the business to hand over, so the incoming Head inherits a running unit rather than a standing start. We are recruiting to take it into its next phase of growth.

The work is running; the structure is not yet. Offerings are defined, collateral exists, engagements are live and Cloudscaler's public voice on applied AI is established. What does not yet exist is the shape around it: there is no ring-fenced team, no separate P&L and no formally defined roles. The unit began with strategy, technical expertise and sales all held in one place. Technical capability has grown since; strategy and commercial ownership have not. Formalising the practice - defining the team, the roles and the commercial structure - is part of the job rather than something the incoming Head inherits finished.

This role has both external and internal responsibilities:

Externally, it owns our AI go-to-market offerings and the customer, partner and pre-sales activity that turns them into pipeline, and it is Cloudscaler's public voice on applied AI.

Internally, it carries full commercial accountability for the business unit, provides technical delivery oversight, builds and leads the practice, and is accountable for enabling the whole company to work with AI.

The role reports to the CTO and works closely with leadership across the business. The person needs to be technical enough to direct and challenge the engineering work, and commercially credible enough to scale the unit and its offering.

It is a hands-on role. In one week, you might write a business case for the Leadership Team, advise a client CTO on their AI strategy, review an engineer's architecture decision and speak at a conference on what we have learned.

External responsibilities

These responsibilities are customer-facing, partner-facing and public facing:

Relentless client focus - Maintaining a relentless client focus, calibrated to how mature the business unit is, and being decisive about where to concentrate effort and what to stop. Early on that means client meetings and pipeline growth; later it means shifting weight to larger, more sustainable areas of demand.

AI go-to-market offerings - Defining and owning our AI go-to-market offerings, working with sales to take them to market. For each offering, defining what it is, who buys it, the problem it solves, its indicative price and its delivery model, and reviewing the set as the market moves, retiring what no longer sells and evolving what does.

Customer relationships - Building trusted-advisor relationships with our customers, from CTOs and CDOs to engineering leaders, advising at every level and translating the same insight into the right language for a C-suite sponsor setting strategy and for the developers implementing it. Converting those relationships into repeat work and referenceable engagements.

Pre-sales leadership - Leading pre-sales activity on AI opportunities, from qualification through to proposal. Supporting the delivery and commercial teams on proposals, workshops and pitches, and leading on bids where applied AI credibility is the differentiator. Qualifying opportunities in or out, including declining those we should not pursue.

Client collateral - Developing reusable client collateral (opportunity assessments, roadmaps and business cases) grounded in real delivery experience. Keeping it current as the offerings and the technology move and making it available to the delivery and commercial teams rather than rebuilt for each deal.

Partner and industry relationships - Building and owning our AI partner and industry relationships (AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI and relevant industry bodies), including the technical relationship, joint go-to-market activity, and achieving and maintaining the respective AI partner competencies that matter to our customers. An existing network inside our partners is a significant advantage, as is fluency in how each organisation works, where it sits in the market and what it is seeking to achieve commercially. Deciding which competencies to pursue and in what order and keeping them current.

Thought leadership and public voice - Providing thought leadership on applied AI and establishing Cloudscaler's public voice through speaking, meetups, blogs and whitepapers. Building our standing in external applied AI communities and contributing to industry discussion, with material grounded in work we have delivered.

Market awareness - Tracking the AI market as it moves - model releases, tooling and emerging frameworks - and forming a clear view on what is credible, what is hype, and what Cloudscaler should adopt. Bringing that view to the Leadership Team early enough to act on it, and setting our position on what we adopt, what we monitor and what we set aside.

Internal responsibilities

These responsibilities cover the commercial, delivery and capability side of the business unit.

Commercial accountability - Carrying full commercial accountability for the business unit, which is run as its own business and measured on clear financial metrics: pipeline, revenue and gross profit. In the first six months that means a six-month revenue plan, with forecast gross profit covering the cost of the leader within six months and the team gross profit positive within two quarters. This grows into full P&L ownership as the unit scales, including team economics that stand on their own.

Reporting and investment cases - Reporting to the Leadership Team on monthly KPIs covering pipeline, utilisation and gross profit against the six-month plan, and building the investment cases that fund the unit's growth. Reporting runs from month one, including the business case for establishing a dedicated team.

Technical delivery oversight - Providing technical delivery oversight of AI customer engagements, working with our delivery teams. This is an architect's role rather than an engineer's: technical enough to hold your own with client engineers and to delegate the detail, and disciplined enough not to commit to capabilities we cannot feasibly deliver. Reviewing architecture and design decisions and acting as the decision-maker when a technical call is needed.

Building and leading the practice - Building and leading our AI practice: owning Cloudscaler's AI strategy and the roadmap to deliver it, hiring and line-managing the team as it grows, capability development, and a repeatable methodology and delivery standards that make quality consistent regardless of who is leading the engagement. Defining the capability model and establishing the practice as an internal centre of excellence for review and quality assurance as it grows.

Decomposing and delegating ownership - Breaking broad areas of activity into distinct responsibilities that can be delegated and genuinely owned, and building the team to hold them. The scope of this role is deliberately broader than one person can carry: the expectation is that the Head of Applied AI grows a team around them - including the AI enablement hires already in train - and leads through that team rather than delivering everything personally. Internal AI usage guidance, reviewing internal projects, pre-sales attendance, marketing campaigns and enablement workshops each need a named owner; an informal approach works while the unit is small but will not scale.

Accelerators and intellectual property - Building reusable AI accelerators and intellectual property that shorten and de-risk customer delivery. Registering the assets as the work matures - accelerators, frameworks and reference architectures - and working with engineering to keep them testable and current as models and tooling evolve. Treating them as Cloudscaler intellectual property with standalone value rather than delivery tools alone.

Company-wide AI enablement - Enabling every Cloudscaler employee to work with AI, including defining our internal AI learning pathways. Setting the guidance for how AI is used in our own work and running the enablement activity that puts it into everyday use across the whole company rather than the practice alone.

Internal community of practice - Growing an internal AI community of practice, giving colleagues outside the team a route to learn and contribute. Running it as a standing forum rather than ad-hoc sessions, so that colleagues outside the practice can build AI capability alongside their own work.

Candidate profile

This is a senior role combining technical depth with commercial ownership. We expect candidates to demonstrate the following:

Technical depth in applied AI - Current, hands-on understanding of AI technologies, models and tooling, sufficient to direct development work, review architecture and design decisions, and hold credible technical conversations with client engineers and architects.

Commercial track record - Experience owning a revenue or gross profit target, building the pipeline behind it, and reporting against a plan. Comfortable being measured on financial outcomes rather than activity.

Consulting and client credibility - A strong communicator who can advise at C-suite level and at engineering level, and whom clients want in the room on their most significant decisions.

Practice or capability building - Experience building a team or capability from a small base: hiring, setting delivery standards, and creating repeatable methodology rather than relying on individual heroics.

Partner ecosystem experience - Familiarity with the AWS and Anthropic ecosystems, or a comparable hyperscaler and model-vendor landscape, including how partner competencies and joint go-to-market activity work in practice.

External profile - A track record of public contribution on applied AI, or the clear appetite and ability to build one.

Leadership and delegation - Experience leading and line-managing a technical team, including setting direction, delegating genuine ownership and developing people. Comfortable achieving outcomes through a team rather than personally delivering the work.

Judgement and prioritisation - The ability to decide where to concentrate a small team's effort, and the discipline to stop work that is not producing.

Benefits

  • Discretionary bonus

  • Discretionary security clearance bonus for those holding certain clearance

  • Periodic offer of share options schemes

  • 25 days’ annual leave

  • 5 additional days per year towards training, certifications, or charity work

  • Option to buy additional annual leave up to 5 days per year

  • Public holidays opt-out scheme, the option to work on public holidays creating the flexibility to enjoy your time off when it suits you

  • Certifications and training expensed

  • Life Assurance

  • Long Term Disability cover

  • Employee Assist Programme for employee advice and support (including legal and counselling helpline)

  • Health, Mental Health, Wellbeing, Financial and Legal support

  • 24/7 GP access

  • Pension auto-enrolment and contribution

  • Employee referral scheme

  • Client referral scheme

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • Travel expenses policy

 

Interview Process

  1. Chat with Talent Team

  2. Remote interview with Hiring Manager

  3. Final in-person with Leadership Team

title: Head of Finance Automation/ AI Agentification
descriptionHtml:
Finance at Rohlik is being rebuilt to run on AI. We already have agents in production that chase overdue payments, process invoices, allocate cash and clear the team's inbox. The pieces work. What we need now is one person to own the whole thing and make it deliver at scale.

 

Role Overview

This is a new role that owns how AI and automation reshape the finance operating model across the Group. You will take a programme that is already live across procure to pay, order to cash and our shared services centre, and turn it from a set of promising experiments into the way finance actually runs.

You report to the Group CFO. You inherit a small team and a live roadmap, and you own the result. You decide what gets automated first, you build and ship with AI tools when that is the fastest way, and you hold every workstream to a number.

The role is deliberately hands on. You should be close enough to the work to build an agent or connect two systems through an API with AI assistance, even though you are not a software developer. You should also be senior enough to redesign how finance works and bring the rest of the business with you.

 

Why this role is exciting

title: Head of Group Reporting
descriptionHtml:
About us

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels. 

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Trainline Group Reporting Team 👋

As a fast moving FTSE 250 business, we're looking for an experienced and technically excellent Head of Group Reporting to join us on a permanent basis. This is a senior role at the heart of our external reporting and financial control framework, calling for deep IFRS expertise and the confidence to navigate complex and judgemental accounting areas. It's a role that goes beyond a typical Group Reporting position, suited to someone who thrives in a varied, fast paced environment, is always ready to get involved, and loves learning new things. Our business changes daily, so we need someone who stays close to the operational side of things and can help us respond quickly and effectively.

Technical rigour is non-negotiable here. You'll be the go-to person for complex and judgemental accounting questions, expected to research positions thoroughly, form a clear view, and defend it with auditors and advisors, while translating that thinking into clear, accessible communication for senior non-financial stakeholders. You'll also bring commercial awareness, particularly around cashflow, liquidity and capital, along with the analytical instinct to spot when the numbers don't add up.

In this role as the Head of Group Reporting, you will...🚄

  • Take ownership of producing the Group's IFRS annual and half yearly listed financial statements and annual report.

  • Lead the year end and half year external audit and review processes end to end, keeping key stakeholders informed and preparing and presenting Audit Committee papers.

  • Oversee the production and filing of subsidiary statutory accounts across our UK and international entities.

  • Own the Group's cashflow forecasting process, providing insight and analysis on liquidity, capital allocation and capital structure to support CFO and Board decision making, working closely with treasury on execution.

  • Act as the Group's primary technical accounting authority, researching and forming well reasoned positions on complex and judgemental areas, implementing new standards, and presenting conclusions to senior management, the Audit Committee, auditors and advisors.

  • Take the lead on one off projects, partnering with teams across the business, while contributing to monthly reporting, annual budgeting, and ownership of specific balance sheet, cashflow and working capital areas.

  • Build and support strong external relationships, including with auditors, loan providers and banking partners, and work closely with legal and CoSec to ensure reporting requirements are met on time.

  • Lead Finance's contribution to the Group's material controls framework under Provision 29, maintain and develop the Group's accounting policies including for acquisitions and legal structure changes, and guide reporting systems and process change to protect the integrity of our control environment.

We'd love to hear from you if you have...🔍

  • You're a qualified accountant with significant post qualification experience, including meaningful time spent in industry within a listed business, and are comfortable with the reporting obligations and scrutiny that come with that environment; you have a consistent record of delivering to deadline.

  • You bring extensive IFRS expertise and a strong technical accounting grounding, confident researching and forming defensible positions on complex areas such as multi-currency consolidations, share based payments, EPS, impairment, revenue recognition, leases and business combinations.

  • If you're currently in practice, you'd be operating at Director level or above, with substantial experience advising listed groups on complex technical matters and be ready to step into a senior in-house leadership role.

  • You have experience researching and implementing new accounting or reporting standards.

  • You're analytical and thorough when reviewing financial information, quick to spot errors in accounting treatment or anomalies that don't add up.

  • You have proven people management experience, with a track record of leading, motivating and developing high performing teams across multiple disciplines.

  • You're an excellent project manager, organised in your own workload while confident delegating and developing others, equally comfortable working independently or as part of a team.

  • You're ambitious and driven, energised by a fast paced environment, always ready to get involved in team projects and try new things; it would be helpful if you're open to occasional travel to our Paris and Edinburgh offices.

More information:

Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits. 

We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one! 

We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy.

Our values represent the things that matter most to us and what we live and breathe everyday, in everything we do: 

  • 💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail 

  • ✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey 

  • 🤝  Travel Together - We're one team 

  • ♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact 

We know that having a diverse team makes us better and helps us succeed. And we mean all forms of diversity - gender, ethnicity, sexuality, disability, nationality and diversity of thought. That's why we're committed to creating inclusive places to work, where everyone belongs and differences are valued and celebrated.

Interested in finding out more about what it's like to work at Trainline? Why not check us out on LinkedIn, Instagram and Glassdoor!

descriptionHtml:

Fanvue is one of the fastest-growing creator monetisation platforms globally. As we grow into payments infrastructure, new verticals and AI tools that work with sensitive data, security has to grow with us.

We're hiring a Head of Security to own security across Fanvue. This is a head-of role, not a CISO. Our technical foundations are in place, built and run by our technical security lead. What we need is someone who owns the decisions around them: who has access to what, which third parties we trust, and whether security gets the focus it needs. You'll set the security roadmap, direct our technical security lead's priorities, and build the team as the function grows.

You'll sit in Operations and work closely with engineering, the People team and every department head. You'll be the person who says "this matters, this needs time" and makes sure it happens.

Access and governance

  • Decide what access each role and team should hold, agree it with department heads and keep it right over time

  • Build the joiner, mover and leaver process with the People team so access follows the org chart

  • Write our security policies and run regular access reviews across every department

  • Work with our technical security lead to turn access decisions into controls

Third parties and certification

  • Approve vendors, tools and AI apps before they touch our data, and keep a live third-party register

  • Run security due diligence on payment and platform partners

  • Lead our path to SOC 2 and ISO 27001, from gap assessment to choosing tooling

Risk and culture

  • Own the security risk register and report on it to the exec team

  • Own the response to security incidents. Engineering incidents and on-call stay with the engineering team

  • Run security awareness across the company, from phishing to safe credential sharing

Roadmap and team

  • Set the security roadmap and direct the priorities of our technical security lead

  • Build the security team as the function grows

📅 Your First Six Months

  • 30 days: handover with our technical security lead and the Ops and People teams. Take over day-to-day security management of our core tools, including Google Workspace, Okta and 1Password

  • 3 months: review access across every role and team in the business and rework it where it needs to change

  • 6 months: the security roadmap and risk register are live and reported on to the exec team, and the function is yours

👀 Who You Are

  • You've owned security at head-of level, with a strong track record to show for it

  • Strong on governance, access management and process, and credible enough with engineers to coordinate technical work

  • Comfortable pushing priorities across departments until they're done

  • Pragmatic. You keep controls tight without slowing the business down

  • A clear communicator who explains risk to non-technical teams and to execs

  • Payments, fintech or high-risk platform experience is a strong plus

  • SOC 2 or ISO 27001 delivery experience is a strong plus

  • AI-forward, you use AI tools in your own workflow

✨ You'll Thrive Here If

  • You want to own security, not advise on it

  • You enjoy building frameworks where there are none yet

  • You're happy being the voice that says security needs time, and holding the line

  • You like working across every team, not just engineering

⚠️ You'll Struggle Here If

  • You want a C-suite title, or need a large team in place before you can be effective

  • You'd rather write infrastructure code than own policy and governance

  • You see controls as a reason to slow the business down

  • You need an established security programme in place before you can be effective

🌍 Why Join Fanvue?

  • Sunday Times Best Places to Work, two years running. We don't just say we have great culture, we prove it

  • Real ownership: you'll be the dedicated owner of security operations and governance, with a direct line to the exec team

  • Fanvue supports hundreds of thousands of creators and millions of fans globally. The problems you solve here are real and immediate

  • Fully remote with unlimited PTO, flexible working hours, a London office and WeWork access when you want it

  • Salary reviews every six months, we don't wait for annual cycles to recognise your growth

  • Travel and office budgets for team off-sites or kitting out your home setup

  • A benefits package we're actively building out, including gym memberships and apps

  • A culture built on innovation, speed, excellence, ownership and transparency

⭐ Fanvue is for Everyone

  • Improve our recruiting model, based on quality over quantity: with the founders, you've sharpened how Vocca hires (who owns what between TA and hiring managers, where we raise the bar, where we cut steps) and turned it into a hiring plan mapped to business needs, by team and by country. Every hire meets the bar, even when volume goes up.

  • A TA team built from scratch: from today's freelance setup to a team of 4 to 6 recruiters by end of 2027, in France and the US, with the right mix of permanent recruiters and freelancers for speed, quality and cost.

  • 60 to 80 hires delivered in 2027 at the expected quality bar.

  • A scalable recruiting system: playbook, scorecards, referrals system, tooling and dashboards live, with tracked KPIs (time-to-hire, offer acceptance, probation validation, quality of hire).

  • AI across the funnel: a recruiting AI strategy you designed and own, with a measurable gain in team productivity.

  • Critical roles closed: senior and critical hires closed by you at first.

  • Autonomous hiring managers: HMs trained on the key recruiting skills, and high satisfaction among HMs and leadership.

  • Employer brand and budget: employer brand live in France and the US, team budget respected.

What you'll own

Strategy and planning

  • Refine the recruiting operating model with the founders

  • Translate the business plan into a hiring plan and a team budget, then own both

Build and lead the TA team

  • Hire your own team (5 to 6 recruiters by end of 2027) across countries, and set the freelance vs permanent mix

  • Train your recruiters until they're autonomous, structure the team, and manage the development of your direct reports

  • Build the playbook, methods, and tooling that make the team scale

AI in recruiting

  • Define and own Vocca's AI strategy for recruiting, from sourcing to closing

  • Test, keep what works, drop what doesn't

Own the hardest hires

  • Recruit senior and critical roles yourself, especially in the US, and know when to delegate and when to own the desk

  • Help hiring managers formalize their needs (scorecards)

  • Build direct sourcing channels that don't always rely on headhunters

  • Run processes end to end

Beyond hiring

  • Train and advise hiring managers on the key recruiting skills

  • Build Vocca's employer brand in France and the US

  • Work with the People team on topics connected to recruiting: key people, onboarding/offboarding, probation validation etc

This role is for you if

Prerequisites:

  • 6+ years in recruiting, including building and leading a TA team in a scaling tech company: you've managed recruiters, set up a playbook and tooling, and managed direct reports.

  • You've deployed AI tools in a real recruiting workflow, and your opinions come from what worked and what failed.

  • Fluent in French and English, based in Paris.

What we'll assess:

  • Business acumen: you understand how a company works, you know the tech market, and you tie hiring to revenue and budget.

  • Data-driven: you diagnose funnel problems with data and make both strategic and operational decisions from it.

  • Ownership: you move without being asked, stay engaged when things get hard, welcome feedback and see things through.

  • Leadership: you know how to sell the company and yourself. Senior candidates see you as Vocca's first showcase, and your team follows you.

  • Multi-country hiring: you can run recruiting across several countries at once, with different markets, comp standards and candidate expectations, even when you're not based there.

Nice to have:

  • A US hiring track record.

  • Experience outside TA: ops, sales, consulting, or building a company.

This role is NOT for you if

  • You want to step away from the desk once your team is in place. Here, you stay close to the hardest hires.

  • You see TA as a support function that executes requests, not a COMEX seat that shapes business and hiring decisions with the founders.

  • AI in recruiting is something you've read about more than used.

Compensation

Perks and benefits

Hiring process

We aim to keep the process within 30 days. You’ll receive continuous feedback throughout.

Why should you join Vocca?

title: HR adviseur Onderwijs
descriptionHtml:
Deze HR functie combineert inhoudelijk advies met coördinatie en verantwoordelijkheid. Als HR adviseur Onderwijs bij Lyceo krijg je de ruimte om inhoudelijk impact te maken én een bredere rol binnen het team te pakken. Je ondersteunt leidinggevenden, begeleidt verzuimtrajecten, verbetert HR processen en coördineert de werkzaamheden binnen het team HR en Salaris. Een veelzijdige volgende stap voor een ervaren HR professional die inhoudelijk sterk is en al ervaring heeft met het begeleiden, coördineren of aansturen van collega's.

Taken

Als HR adviseur Onderwijs ondersteun je leidinggevenden bij personele vraagstukken, begeleid je verzuimtrajecten en denk je mee over beleid en organisatieontwikkeling. Tegelijkertijd zorg je voor overzicht en samenhang binnen het team HR en Salaris. Je coördineert de werkzaamheden binnen het team en bent verantwoordelijk voor recruitment, waarbij je ook de recruiter begeleidt en aanstuurt.

Je blijft nadrukkelijk zelf actief in de dagelijkse HR praktijk. De ene dag begeleid je een leidinggevende bij een complex verzuimdossier, de andere dag stem je prioriteiten binnen het team af, bespreek je de voortgang van recruitment of werk je aan nieuw HR beleid. Zo verbind je HR beleid, processen en de dagelijkse praktijk met elkaar. Je kent de dynamiek van de organisatie, weet wat er op de verschillende vestigingen speelt en zorgt ervoor dat het team effectief inspeelt op wat de organisatie nodig heeft.

Kortom, jij pakt de regie bij het:

  • adviseren van leidinggevenden en management over HR en organisatievraagstukken;
  • begeleiden van verzuimtrajecten, waaronder complexe en langdurige dossiers;
  • ontwikkelen, implementeren en evalueren van HR-beleid en optimaliseren en borgen van HR-processen;
  • coördineren van de werkzaamheden binnen het team HR en Salaris, inclusief recruitment, en het begeleiden en aansturen van collega's binnen het team;
  • goed gevoel voor relevante wet en regelgeving rond arbeidsrecht, verzuim en beloning, en het vermogen om tijdig juridische of fiscale aandachtspunten te signaleren.

Vereisten

Voor deze vacature neem jij mee:

Je bent een stevige HR professional die zelfstandig werkt, overzicht houdt en gemakkelijk schakelt tussen verschillende gesprekspartners. Je voelt je prettig in een rol waarin je adviseert, zaken voor elkaar krijgt en collega's begeleidt. Daarbij combineer je een proactieve, praktische en resultaatgerichte instelling met een uitstekende beheersing van de Nederlandse taal.

Vink jij deze checklist ook af?

  • hbo werk- en denkniveau en een afgeronde HR-gerelateerde opleiding;
  • minimaal 3 jaar ervaring als HR adviseur;
  • voldoende kennis van arbeidsrecht, de Wet verbetering poortwachter en fiscaliteit rond beloningssystematiek;
  • ervaring met verzuimtrajecten;
  • affiniteit met het ontwikkelen van beleid en het verbeteren van processen.

Jouw werkgebied

Jouw nieuwe werkplek bevindt zich in Leiden, op tien minuten lopen van Leiden Centraal. Dankzij deze centrale ligging is het kantoor uitstekend bereikbaar met het openbaar vervoer. Vanuit Leiden werk je nauw samen met leidinggevenden, management en jouw directe HR-collega’s. De functie biedt daarmee een centrale uitvalsbasis voor jouw werk binnen de organisatie.

Benefits

Als gedreven HR adviseur kun jij rekenen op:

Veel ruimte om zelfstandig te werken en verantwoordelijkheid te nemen bij een organisatie met korte lijnen, waar goede ideeën snel besproken én uitgevoerd kunnen worden. Je komt terecht in een betrokken team waarin samenwerken, kennis delen en eigenaarschap centraal staan. Ook krijg je volop ruimte om jezelf verder te ontwikkelen.

Op basis van een fulltime dienstverband krijg je daarbovenop:

Werken bij Lyceo

Wie werkt bij Lyceo, blijft leren. Lyceo is marktleider in aanvullend onderwijs en helpt jaarlijks duizenden leerlingen met huiswerkbegeleiding, examentrainingen, bijspijkertrajecten en andere onderwijsprogramma’s. title: Identity Product Manager
descriptionHtml:
Who is Sonar?

Sonar enables organizations to ship agentic code with confidence. Code creation is abundant, but confidence is scarce. Our core platform, SonarQube, verifies over 750 billion lines of code every day, delivering agentic verification and governance for all code. Trusted by more than 7 million developers and 75% of the Fortune 100, including teams at Nvidia, ServiceNow, Booking.com, Goldman Sachs, AstraZeneca, and Ford Motor Company, Sonar enables organizations to reduce outages, improve security, and lower the cost and risk of agentic software development.

Founded in Geneva and now headquartered in Austin, Texas, Sonar has a global team working across offices and hubs, including Silicon Valley, London, Bochum, Barcelona, Singapore, Tokyo, and the Washington, D.C. area. At Sonar, we’re enabling enterprises to build agentic software factories that can move quickly while maintaining the control, consistency and evidence required to ship with confidence.


Position description

Sonar is looking for a customer-centric Identity Product Manager to drive the authentication, authorization, and access management capabilities that let every user, from an individual developer to the largest regulated enterprise, get into Sonar products securely and without friction. You will work with the Identity squad, in the Storefront domain, which provides the operational foundation enabling seamless customer access to Sonar's products, underpinning core business processes such as billing and entitlement.

This role sits at the intersection of customer experience, security, and compliance. As a Product Manager, you will shape how organizations authenticate into Sonar (SSO via SAML/OIDC, with enterprise identity providers such as Okta and Entra ID), how permissions and roles are managed at scale, and how user and organization identities are provisioned and kept secure throughout their lifecycle. To achieve this, we need a passionate Product Manager who will research, clarify, and prioritize the needs of external IT administrators, security teams, and enterprise buyers, and translate those needs across our product line.

You will join the Product Management team, composed of other passionate Product Managers eager to collaborate with you. You will also work closely with the Identity engineering teams to ensure that proposed solutions meet the expected outcome, and that we collectively deliver an identity experience that is both secure by default and simple for administrators to operate at scale.

By joining us, you will bring your deep knowledge of identity and access management (SSO, IdP integrations, RBAC/permissions, user provisioning) and your experience as a Product Manager to help us reach the next level and provide a trusted, frictionless experience to millions of developers and thousands of enterprise administrators.


What you will do

  • Contribute to the different areas of the Identity vision and communicate about them, internally and externally.

  • Research, clarify, and prioritize opportunities to build and maintain an effective roadmap, focused on enterprise-grade authentication, authorization, and access management.

  • Interact directly with our users and customers to support them, integrate their feedback, and identify opportunities.

  • Develop a deep understanding of enterprise identity needs (e.g., SSO/SAML/OIDC, IdP integrations such as Okta and Entra ID, SCIM/user provisioning, and fine-grained permissions) and how we can enable organizations to onboard and administer users at scale.

  • Drive modernization of enterprise identity and access management, including expanding IdP support and hardening permissions and role management for the largest, most complex organizations.

  • Work closely with other product managers to design cross-product features.

  • Align with the engineering and UX teams on the problems to solve and support them during the end-to-end development stage of the solutions.

  • Sync with the engineering teams to ensure that there is a good balance between innovation, consolidation, and stability.

  • Attend conferences and give talks if you like.

  • Help the Product Management team grow in its organization, tools, and processes.


    • Experience and qualifications

  • Passionate about identity and access management, and the practices that lead to seamless and secure authentication systems.

  • Deep understanding of identity protocols and patterns (e.g., SAML, OIDC/OAuth2, SSO, SCIM/provisioning, JWT) and enterprise identity providers (Okta, Entra ID/Azure AD, or similar).

  • Technical comprehension of permissions and access control models (RBAC/ABAC) and multi-tenant SaaS access control.

  • Understanding of the compliance and security expectations of enterprise buyers (e.g., SOC 2) as they relate to identity and access.

  • Experience with the latest developments in AI assisted coding.

  • Experience in software product management, preferably managing identity in an agile context.

  • Highly autonomous and pragmatic, with an obsession for solving external customer problems.

  • Open-minded and very positive can-do attitude.

  • Comfortable in dealing with change, complexity, and uncertainty.

  • Self-confident enough to challenge the status quo as well as to receive feedback.

  • Leadership: you take initiative and demonstrate your ability to lead a subject from beginning to end.

title: Infrastructure / Platform Engineer (London)
descriptionHtml:
Location: London, UK

Type: Full-time, in office

About Neuphonic

Neuphonic is building the next generation of voice AI, making natural, real-time speech accessible across devices, languages, and applications.

Our technology enables ultra-low-latency text-to-speech, voice cloning, and multilingual speech generation. We're pushing the boundaries of what's possible with speech models, from high-performance cloud inference to running AI directly on everyday devices without expensive GPUs or an internet connection.

We're a small, ambitious team of researchers and engineers building technology used by developers and businesses around the world. Our open-source releases have reached millions of downloads, and we're growing quickly.

Why we're hiring

As our customer base grows, we need to scale our production infrastructure while maintaining the performance, reliability, and low latency that our products depend on.

We're looking for an Infrastructure / Platform Engineer to take ownership of our cloud infrastructure and inference systems. You'll work closely with our engineering and ML teams to build scalable, reliable, and cost-efficient systems.

What you'll own

  • Cloud infrastructure: Build, manage, and scale our production infrastructure across GCP and GPU cloud providers using Kubernetes, Docker, and Terraform.

  • Inference optimisation: Continuously improve inference performance, latency, throughput, GPU utilisation, and infrastructure costs through profiling, experimentation, and iteration, rather than simply maintaining the status quo.

  • Platform evolution: Identify bottlenecks and inefficiencies in how we build, deploy, and serve models, and take ownership of implementing improvements.

  • Production reliability: Monitor critical systems, respond to incidents, and help ensure reliable service for our customers outside UK working hours.

  • Infrastructure architecture: Make autonomous technical decisions that balance scalability, reliability, performance, and cost.

  • CI/CD and automation: Improve deployment pipelines, infrastructure automation, monitoring, and observability.

  • Security and enterprise readiness: Support secure infrastructure practices and enterprise deployment requirements.

What we're looking for

  • Strong experience building and operating production cloud infrastructure at scale, ideally supporting applications with significant user traffic.

  • Hands-on experience with GCP, Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, and Python.

  • Experience with CI/CD, monitoring, observability, and production incident response.

  • A strong understanding of infrastructure performance, scalability, and cost optimisation.

  • Experience participating in on-call rotations or taking responsibility for production incidents.

  • A proactive approach to engineering, with experience identifying bottlenecks, experimenting with improvements, and optimising production systems.

  • Comfortable working autonomously, making architectural decisions, and taking ownership of critical systems.

Nice to have

  • Experience with AI/ML inference, GPU infrastructure, or vLLM.

  • Experience hosting audio, speech, or real-time AI applications.

  • Experience with C++.

  • Familiarity with SOC 2, ISO 27001, or other security compliance frameworks.

  • Experience with private cloud or on-premise enterprise deployments.

Who you'll work with

You'll work directly with our engineering and ML teams, helping shape the infrastructure behind Neuphonic's production models and services.

We're a small team, so you'll have real ownership and the freedom to make meaningful technical decisions. We value people who take initiative, solve problems independently, and enjoy building systems that work reliably in the real world.

title: Inside Sales Representative - EMEA
descriptionHtml:
Are you passionate, enthusiastic, and looking for an opportunity to grow your career in sales? Are you looking for your next challenge in an emerging and exciting market? If yes then we want to hear from you!

The impact you will have:

You will join our EMEA Commercial team, part of Elliptic's global Commercial organisation, and champion uncovering and developing new customer relationships across EMEA. As an Inside Sales Representative you will become an expert in Elliptic's value proposition, helping both prospective and existing customers navigate and enter the digital asset market with your knowledge of our product and of the compliance and regulatory environment.

You will own the full sales cycle for new business in the Growth segment, and you will grow the customers already in your patch in two ways: up-sell, expanding what an existing customer already buys as their usage and licence needs grow, and cross-sell, introducing Elliptic products they do not yet use. You will manage the full cycle including prospecting, qualifying, developing proposals, negotiating terms and closing.

This is an opportunity to build a career in a market you can shape as well as sell into. Fascinating and challenging work is the norm - working at Elliptic is never boring!

What you will do:

  • Run the full sales cycle, from pipeline generation to deal closure, across a territory with massive potential and that has considerable inbound interest.

  • Develop net new business and cross sell opportunities across the Growth segment within EMEA

  • Build out strategic market penetration plan, prospect, and manage full sales cycle

  • Use AI tooling to work a patch of 1,000+ Growth accounts at scale: researching and segmenting accounts, building and iterating outbound motions, and drafting personalised outreach at volume without losing quality.

  • Proactively contact prospects to identify & qualify sales opportunities.

  • Prospect and generate high quality leads

  • Develop custom proposals based on customer requirements

  • Conduct presentations and product demos

  • Negotiate terms and close the business

  • Work with Customer Success to review licence utilisation and product adoption across the accounts in your patch, using that data to identify and run up-sell and cross-sell plays, with ownership agreed per account with the CSM.

  • Be an ambassador of the Elliptic brand, living our values of curiosity, trust, and action in every interaction.

  • Own your number: meet and exceed quarterly and annual quota, keep an accurate and current forecast with all sales pipeline and activity managed in CRM, and drive linearity so revenue lands consistently through the quarter rather than in the closing weeks.

What you will achieve in the first 6 months:

  • Completed Elliptic's product certifications and onboarding processes.

  • Mapped your territory and built a qualified pipeline of at least 3x your quarterly quota through a combination of inbound, outbound, and partner-sourced opportunities.

  • Established a recurring utilisation review with your CSM counterpart covering your patch, with a standing list of up-sell and cross-sell plays ranked by adoption signal.

  • Run complete discovery cycles, using the Value Pyramid to connect client pain points to our solutions, applying MEDDPPICC to qualify or disqualify with confidence, and have a clear view of what you're walking away from and why.

  • Mapped and segmented your patch of 1,000+ accounts, and built qualified pipeline coverage of 3x your New Business quarterly target and 2x your Expansion quarterly target, through open opportunities sourced across inbound, outbound and partner routes.

  • Established a repeatable weekly rhythm that produces a consistent monthly close rate, closing new business every month rather than in end-of-quarter bursts, so that by the end of your first six months you are in a position to hit and exceed your quarterly target.

You will be a great fit here if you are:

  • A driven, tenacious “hunter” who thrives on owning their number and finding creative ways to meet and exceed it.

  • Experience in B2B SaaS and/or DaaS sales within RegTech, FinTech, and/or Crypto.

  • Commercially curious, you ask smart questions, seek to understand the "why" behind a customer’s problems, and use those insights to tailor impactful solutions.

  • Confident, consultative, and persuasive, able to build strong stakeholder relationships at all levels, from mid-level managers to C-suites.

  • A collaborative team player, independent yet never a “lone wolf.” You value and engage support from your pack.

  • Agile, resourceful, and fearless, you see opportunities where others see blockers and know how to create inroads where none appear to exist.

  • Can understand the customer’s business model, and how digital assets fit into their strategy

  • Have the ability to analyse data to identify market trends and opportunities for cryptocurrency and compliance

  • Can evaluate customer needs and preferences in relation to pricing, product terms and conditions to ensure that client requirements are addressed in commercial proposals

  • Enjoy working with pace and energy, building team spirit and cultivating unity and commitment among the team

  • Have an understanding of complex B2B sales methodologies

  • Are a self-starter, adaptable and comfortable with changing priorities

  • Proven experience and knowledge of use of AI tools into day-to-day workflows

Our ideal candidate has:

  • Strong outbound prospecting skills, with a track record of generating net new business and pipeline growth

  • Demonstrated track record of success and quota over achievement

  • A strong work ethic and an entrepreneur’s mindset. You’re comfortable creating value in a low structure environment while being agile and resilient

  • Minimum baseline understanding about digital assets and the crypto economy

  • Familiarity with the MEDDPPICC methodology and Value Based Selling.

  • Proficiency in CRM systems (HubSpot or similar), LLMs and other AI-driven prospecting and work efficiency tools.

  • Passionate about agentic AI and excited to help customers navigate a rapidly evolving industry.

Bonus Points for:

  • Intimate understanding of AML/KYC and Forensics space, either in cryptocurrency or traditional financial environments

  • Experience selling SaaS solutions to crypto-native financial services business

  • Fluency / business level in European language(s)

  • A proven use case and understanding of agentic AI is a strong plus.

How We Work

  • Hybrid working and the option to work from almost anywhere for up to 90 days per year

  • £500 Remote working budget to set up your home office space

Learning & Development:

  • £1,000 Learning & Development budget to use on anything (agreed with your manager) that contributes to your growth and development

Vacation/ Leave:

  • Holidays: 25 days of annual leave + bank holidays

  • An extra day for your birthday

  • Enhanced parental leave: we provide eligible employees, regardless of gender or whether they become a parent by birth or adoption, 16 weeks fully-paid leave and leave.

Benefits:

  • Private Health Insurance - we use Bupa!

  • Full access to Spill Mental Health Support

  • Life Assurance: we hope you will never need this - but our cover is for 4 times your salary to your beneficiaries

  • Cycle to Work Scheme

We know Diversity and Inclusion is much deeper than just hiring, but it’s important for us to mention it here. We welcome and embrace individuals of all backgrounds and identities at Elliptic, and this is an ongoing priority for us. We know incredible people don’t all think in the same way. We want to be challenged every day. We believe our diverse team of individuals underpins this by bringing creative thinking and innovation to Elliptic every day. We are committed to creating a diverse, inclusive and equitable workplace, so we welcome applications from everyone, even if you may not think you fit all of the requirements of our roles. We foster an environment of psychological safety, where everyone feels comfortable to bring their whole self to work.

Ultimately we are looking to hire those who want to be the future leaders in the industry, super intrigued by Crypto and have an awesome mindset to learn so if you don’t meet all the criteria still do apply!

title: Insurance Compliance Counsel
descriptionHtml:
Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

The Role

Alan’s Insurance Compliance Counsel, you will be Alan's expert on insurance compliance and consumer protection regulation. You will define how regulatory obligations translate into Alan's tools, processes, and products. You will own the compliance posture on your perimeter, proactively manage our exposure, and be the primary interface with regulators on the topics you cover.

You will also be a key connector between the compliance function, internal control, and the audit processes Alan conducts - ensuring audit findings are properly digested, remediated, and embedded into how we operate.

As Alan expands into new markets, you will play a central role in ensuring our compliance standards travel with us: adapting Group frameworks to local requirements and helping stand up the right compliance foundations in new geographies.

The role sits within the Legal Area in the Corporate Unit, and involves close daily collaboration with the Legal, Insurance, Operations, Sales, Care, and Product teams across all of Alan's markets.

 

What You Will Do

Own Alan's Insurance Compliance Posture

  • Define how regulatory obligations relating to Alan’s core product (IDD including duty of advice, product governance, AML/CFT, etc.) translate into Alan's operational processes, product design, and tooling

  • Suggest optimal ways to meet regulatory requirements within Alan's products while improving members' experience - from pricing components and options design to UX choices and complaint handling

  • Proactively identify compliance risks, assess their exposure, and develop mitigating action plans in coordination with internal stakeholders

  • Lead the structuring and continuous improvement of Alan's complaints management framework across France, Belgium, and Spain, ensuring compliance with ACPR recommendations and local equivalents

Reporting & Audits

  • Serve as the compliance function's key contributor to Alan's internal control system: document compliance-related risks and controls in the Group's centralised mapping, and co-deploy the internal control approach across teams (Insurance, Operations, Sales, Care)

  • Prepare and support internal and external audits: assess Alan's standing against planned operational improvements, define remediation plans, and drive and monitor their effective implementation

  • Report on compliance obligations and risk exposure to Alan's Board and governance committees, with clarity and foresight; Manage regulatory reporting obligations including the ACPR Questionnaire Protection de la Clientèle (QPC)

  • Respond to regulatory inspections (ACPR, FSMA, or equivalent in Alan’s operating countries), coordinating internally and ensuring Alan is always audit-ready

AML/CFT & KYC

  • Support the AML framework: conduct second-level analysis on suspicious cases, manage relationships with regulatory bodies and financial intelligence units, approve high-risk client relationships (including PEPs), and maintain the AML/CFT risk assessment framework

  • Oversee KYC Ops referents' training and upskilling, including Belgium-specific AML requirements

  • Coordinate with the AMLO on annual priorities, documentation, monitoring tools, and regulatory reporting to the ACPR and equivalent supervisors

Compliance Roadmap & Stakeholder Coordination

  • Maintain Alan's compliance roadmap: prioritise, track progress, update the risk mapping, and re-prioritise as the regulatory environment evolves

  • Lead compliance projects with internal stakeholders across Insurance, Product, Sales, Care, and Operations, translating regulatory requirements into concrete deliverables and timelines

  • Contribute to pragmatic compliance positions on regulatory requirements that affect our products and contracts - turning complex constraints into well-reasoned, pragmatic solutions that support the business.

Regulatory Training & Internal Capability

  • Design and maintain mandatory regulatory training programmes for Sales and Care roles (IDD competency requirements including duty of advice and product governance, Loi Evin, AML/CFT)

  • Build internal compliance frameworks, guidelines, and decision-making tools that increase team autonomy and reduce reliance on external resources

  • Contribute to Alan's written culture by producing high-quality documentation that teams can rely on independently

International Compliance & Localisation

  • Ensure Alan's compliance standards travel consistently across all Group markets, whether existing (France, Belgium, Spain, Canada) or newly opened, adapting Group frameworks to local regulatory requirements and deploying them locally in coordination with local counsel.

 

Profile

Experience & Skills

  • 4+ years of experience in compliance in an insurance or fintech company; solid coverage of at least two of the following: AML/CFT, insurance distribution (IDD), complaints handling, regulatory reporting

  • Solid understanding of the French insurance regulatory framework and ability to work across EU/local requirements

  • Proven ability to lead compliance projects cross-functionally: you translate regulatory requirements into clear priorities, align internal stakeholders, and deliver without creating bottlenecks or increased friction

  • Bilingual French/English (both required, written and spoken)

  • International exposure is a strong plus

You Will Thrive Here If You Are

  • A pragmatic problem-solver: you find the right answer within regulatory constraints rather than defaulting to the most conservative one

  • Rigorous and well-organised: you maintain high documentation standards, track your commitments, and keep stakeholders informed

  • Business-minded: you understand what matters for the company's growth and your members' protection, and you calibrate your compliance work accordingly

🎯 Important note: we hire people, not roles.

If you're excited about this opportunity but don't check every box, we'd love to hear from you. Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply, as it can only bring learnings or success.

If you identify yourself as a woman: Did you know that research shows women often apply only when meeting 100% of requirements?

Remember, this is just a guide, not a checklist. We'll be thrilled to receive your application!

 

🔖 Check out our About Alan and Career pages, as well as our Medium, blog and Glassdoor page for more info.

 

You want to know more about Alan?

  • 🙌 Perks & Benefits: Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers.

  • 🤘 A strong culture: People joining Alan are often surprised and delighted by our innovative working method. We have a set of cultural values that guide our approach to work

title: Intern - AI Financial Advisory (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Über Finton

Finton ist eine AI-Native Finance-Beratung, die AI-gestützte Lösungen für den CFO-Bereich konzipiert und implementiert. Unsere Services erbringen wir mit unserer eigenen Software, die den Berater von Projektmanagement über Datenverarbeitung bis zu Datenanalyse und Dashboard-Erstellung durchgängig mit AI unterstützt.

Konkret heißt das: Wir setzen auf dem bestehenden ERP, der Buchhaltung und den operativen Systemen des Kunden auf, bringen die Daten zusammen und liefern in kürzester Zeit ein produktives Ergebnis, etwa ein monatliches Management Reporting mit Kommentierung, einen rollierenden 13-Wochen-Cash-Forecast, eine Deckungsbeitrags- und Umsatzanalyse nach Kunden, Produkten oder Projekten oder einen Datenraum und ein Financial Fact Book für eine anstehende Transaktion.

Daneben arbeiten wir klassisch beratend: als Sparringspartner des CFO bei Budget, Forecast und Investorenkommunikation, als Interim-Kapazität in der Finanzabteilung und als Unterstützung bei M&A, Fundraising und Due-Diligence-Vorbereitung.

Unsere Kunden sind mittelständische und investorenfinanzierte Unternehmen mit typischerweise 10 bis 250 Mio. Euro Umsatz, bei denen das Finance-Team für die Anforderungen von Gesellschaftern und Banken zu klein oder zu manuell aufgestellt ist.

Finton wurde 2023 von Jan, Julian und Neil gegründet und betreut Kunden in der gesamten DACH-Region von Hamburg, Köln und München aus. Mehr als 150 abgeschlossene Projekte sprechen für sich.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Projektunterstützung: Du arbeitest im Hintergrund in laufenden Kundenprojekten mit: Du bereitest Finanzdaten aus ERP und Buchhaltung auf, baust Auswertungen und Dashboards auf unserer AI-Plattform und lieferst dem Projektteam die Grundlage für das Gespräch mit dem CFO.

  • Finanzmodelle und Analysen: Du wirkst an Finanzmodellen, Cash Forecasts, Deckungsbeitragsanalysen und Unternehmensbewertungen mit und prüfst Daten und Ergebnisse auf Plausibilität.

  • Business Development: Du recherchierst Zielkunden, Investoren und Multiplikatoren, pflegst unsere Lead-Listen und erstellst Angebots- und Pitch-Unterlagen sowie Case Studies.

  • Strategie: Du arbeitest direkt mit den Gründern an strategischen Fragen wie Positionierung, Pricing, neuen Service-Linien und Partnerschaften, von der Analyse bis zur Entscheidungsvorlage.

  • Markt- und Wettbewerbsanalyse: Du beobachtest Markt, Wettbewerber und AI-Entwicklungen im Finance-Bereich und leitest daraus Empfehlungen für unser Angebot ab.

  • Produktentwicklung: Mit deinem Feedback aus Projektarbeit und Markt hilfst du unserem Technologie-Team, die AI-Plattform weiterzuentwickeln.

  • Eigeninitiative: Du gestaltest mit, statt nur abzuarbeiten, auch bei internen Themen wie Recruiting, Wissensaufbau oder Prozessverbesserung.

Das bringst Du mit

  • Studium: Laufendes oder abgeschlossenes Bachelor- oder Masterstudium der Wirtschaftswissenschaften, des Wirtschaftsingenieurwesens oder eine vergleichbare Fachrichtung mit sehr guten Leistungen, mindestens drei abgeschlossene Semester.

  • Erfahrung: Erste relevante Praxiserfahrung, etwa durch Praktika in Consulting, Investment Banking, Transaction Advisory, Private Equity oder in der Finanzabteilung eines Unternehmens.

  • Handwerk: Sicherer Umgang mit Excel und PowerPoint, Grundverständnis von Bilanz, GuV und Cashflow; erste Berührung mit Finanzmodellen oder Bewertung ist ein Plus.

  • Technologie: Interesse an AI und Prozessautomatisierung im Finanzwesen. Programmierkenntnisse sind kein Muss, aber du willst verstehen, wie unsere Lösungen funktionieren.

  • Analytik: Starke analytische Fähigkeiten, strukturierte Arbeitsweise und ein gutes betriebswirtschaftliches Verständnis.

  • Haltung: Eigeninitiative, Zuverlässigkeit und Freude daran, in einem kleinen Team Dinge selbst voranzutreiben.

  • Sprachen: Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.

Deine ersten Monate bei Finton

In den ersten Tagen lernst du unsere Plattform, unsere Projektmethodik und unsere laufenden Mandate kennen und bekommst einen festen Ansprechpartner im Team. Schon in der ersten Woche unterstützt du ein Kundenprojekt aus dem Hintergrund: Du bereitest Daten auf, baust erste Auswertungen und siehst, wie aus Rohdaten ein Reporting für den CFO wird.

Nach den ersten Wochen übernimmst du eigene Arbeitspakete, etwa einen Teil eines Finanzmodells, eine Wettbewerbsanalyse oder den Aufbau einer neuen Lead-Liste, und präsentierst deine Ergebnisse direkt den Gründern.

Benefits

  • Echte Aufgaben statt Zuschauen: Du arbeitest an realen Projekten, Modellen und Strategiethemen mit und siehst, was mit deiner Arbeit beim Kunden passiert. Kein Kaffeekochen, kein Folienschubsen ohne Kontext.

  • Direkter Draht zu den Gründern: Du bekommst einen festen Mentor aus dem Gründerteam, regelmäßiges Feedback und Einblick, wie eine Beratung aufgebaut und geführt wird.

  • Perspektive: Wer überzeugt, hat die Option, nach dem Praktikum in Vollzeit bei uns einzusteigen.

  • Vergütung: Eine faire Praktikumsvergütung, die deine Erfahrung berücksichtigt.

  • Technologie: Du arbeitest mit unserer eigenen AI-Plattform statt mit Excel-Handarbeit und lernst, wie Finance- und Beratungsarbeit in den nächsten Jahren aussehen wird.

  • Standort Köln: Unser Büro liegt am Friesenplatz, mitten in der Stadt. Wir arbeiten gemeinsam vor Ort, weil du so am schnellsten lernst und wir als kleines Team schnell entscheiden wollen. Flexible Arbeitszeiten gehören dazu.

  • Ausstattung und Extras: Firmenlaptop, Zuschuss zum ÖPNV-Ticket, Fitnessabo, kostenlose Getränke im Büro, lockere Kleiderordnung sowie regelmäßige Teamevents und Firmenfeiern in einem kleinen Team mit flachen Hierarchien.

Bewerbung

Wenn du diesen Weg mitgestalten willst, freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung über die Plattform. Ein Lebenslauf reicht uns für den Anfang; ein Anschreiben brauchst du nicht. Du hörst innerhalb von einer Woche von uns, und dein erstes Gespräch führst du direkt mit einem der Gründer.

title: Intern Data Analyst - Paris
descriptionHtml:
Qui sommes-nous ?

Fondée en 2014, Artefact est une société française de services autour de la data, spécialisée dans le conseil en IA, transformation data et en data & digital marketing. L’approche unique d’Artefact, qui fait le pont entre la donnée et le business, permet à nos clients d’atteindre leurs objectifs business de façon dédiée et efficace. Nos 2500 collaborateurs répartis dans 27 bureaux à travers le monde allient leurs compétences pluridisciplinaires au profit de l’innovation business des entreprises.

La mission des Artefactors ? Transformer la data de nos clients en impact business. Dans ce sens, nous collaborons avec plus de 1000 clients, leaders de leurs industries (Orange, Carrefour, Samsung, AccorHotels, L’Oréal, LVMH, Decathlon) et sommes partenaires privilégiés de Google (GMP/GCP), AWS ainsi que Microsoft Azure.

En tant que stagiaire Data Analyst, tu seras intégré(e) à une équipe travaillant étroitement avec des consultants / data scientists et tu participeras à des missions ayant un impact réel pour les clients. Tes missions pourront inclure :

  • Collecter, nettoyer, préparer les données à partir de sources diverses (bases de données internes, API, logs, etc.).

  • Explorer et analyser les données pour identifier tendances, anomalies, corrélations, patterns utiles.

  • Participer à la conception et réalisation de dashboards / reportings sous outils de data visualisation (ex. Tableau, PowerBI, ou outils internes) pour présenter les résultats aux équipes ou aux clients.

  • Contribuer à la définition de KPI pertinents selon les objectifs métier.

  • Travailler en collaboration avec les équipes métier (marketing, produit, etc.) pour bien comprendre leurs besoins et transformer ces besoins en analyses exploitables.

  • Aider à automatiser certains processus de reporting ou analyses simples.

  • Documenter tes travaux, partager les résultats et les apprentissages au sein de l’équipe, proposer des améliorations ou de nouvelles approches quand c’est possible.

Profil recherché

  • Étudiant(e) en dernière année de cycle ingénieur, Master 2, ou équivalent, avec une spécialisation en Data, Intelligence Artificielle, Mathématiques appliquées, Statistiques ou Informatique et recherche un stage de fin d'études à partir de Janvier 2027.

  • Maîtrise de SQL pour extraire / manipuler les données.

  • Connaissances en langage de programmation pour l’analyse de données, typiquement Python (avec pandas, numpy, etc.).

  • Bonne compréhension des principes statistiques de base (moyennes, distributions, tests, corrélations, variance, etc.).

  • Capacité à créer des visualisations / dashboards (Tableau, PowerBI, ou outil équivalent).

  • Connaissance minimale de l’écosystème numérique et data (web analytics, datalake, dataviz, etc.) est un plus.

Compétences personnelles / soft skills :

  • Esprit logique et analytique, souci du détail.

  • Sens de la communication orale et écrite : savoir expliquer ses résultats à des non-experts.

  • Capacité à travailler en équipe, à écouter et à comprendre les besoins métier.

  • Proactivité, curiosité, et capacité à proposer des idées ou des approches nouvelles.

  • Autonomie, tout en étant à l’aise avec le suivi et les retours.

  • Bon niveau en français (oral et écrit) ; l’anglais professionnel est un plus, notamment pour échanges ou documentations. 

Ce que nous offrons

  • Un stage de 6 mois basé à Paris dans le 9ème arrondissement 
  • Un accompagnement par un tuteur expérimenté et l'opportunité de travailler avec des équipes reconnues 
  • La possibilité d'être embauché(e) en CDI à l'issue du stage 
  • Socle de formation (training day, Retex, café tech) développement des compétences via des outils internes innovants 

Prêt à rejoindre l'aventure ?

Si tu te reconnais dans cette description et que tu souhaites mettre tes compétences au service de projets concrets et impactants, envoie-nous ta candidature !

Chez Artefact, nous recrutons nos collaborateurs uniquement en fonction de nos besoins et des qualités propres de chaque candidat. Nous assurons le développement de leurs compétences professionnelles et de leurs responsabilités sans discrimination d’aucune sorte. Le groupe s'engage à reconnaître et promouvoir tous les talents, quels que soient leurs croyances, âge, handicap, parentalité, origine ethnique, nationalité, identité de genre, orientation sexuelle, appartenance à une organisation politique, religieuse, syndicale ou à une minorité, ou toute autre caractéristique qui pourrait faire l'objet d'une discrimination.

We’re looking for an Internal Communications Manager to strengthen the communication that keeps Legora aligned, informed, and moving quickly as we scale globally.

Over approximately 12 months, you’ll take ownership of our internal communications strategy, channels, and cadence. You’ll turn complex information into clear, useful communication, and help translate company priorities into shared understanding and action.

Reporting to the Senior Communications Director EMEA, you’ll work closely with the leadership team, Head of Operations, VP Marketing, and teams across Product, Engineering, Go-to-Market, and People. Your focus will be making sure decisions land well, context is shared at the right time, and our culture remains strong as we grow.

Your Mandate

Create clarity, alignment, and momentum across a fast-moving organization—with as little friction and noise as possible.

What You’ll Do

Internal Communications Strategy & Operating Rhythm

  • Execute the internal communications strategy: audiences, messages, channels, and tone.

  • Manage a scalable comms operating rhythm (weekly updates, leadership notes, All-Hands/Townhalls, Q&A formats).

  • Ensure the right information reaches the right people at the right time — without noise.

Leadership & Change Communications

  • Partner with leadership to shape narratives and craft clear updates on priorities, decisions, and progress.

  • Lead communications for organizational change: new processes, policy changes, major launches.

  • Build trust through transparency and consistency, especially during ambiguity.

Improve Channels, Content & Knowledge Flow

  • Own and continuously improve internal communications channels (e.g., Slack, Notion)

  • Produce crisp, useful content: announcements, FAQs, decision summaries, “what changed” notes, playbooks.

  • Create templates and standards that help teams communicate clearly and consistently.

Strengthen Culture and Engagement

  • Capture and amplify what matters: wins, learnings, customer impact, and how we work.

  • Strengthen culture and collaboration across teams and geographies through thoughtful storytelling and rituals.

  • Track engagement and effectiveness, then iterate based on what people actually need.

Who You Are

You’re driven by clarity, pace, and simplicity. You are an excellent listener, and you love taking messy inputs and making them easy to understand without losing nuance.

You thrive in fast-changing environments, bring structure where it’s needed, and have strong judgment on what to communicate, when, and how.

You Are

  • A sharp, confident writer who is equally strong in short-form (Slack) and long-form (narratives, memos).

  • Highly proactive and independent, with excellent prioritization.

  • Comfortable working closely with leadership.

  • Curious about AI and excited to use tools to communicate smarter (not louder).

What We’re Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience in internal communications, corporate communications or similar roles in high-growth environments.

  • Strong project management skills and a process-oriented mindset.

Why This Role Matters

Legora is growing quickly. During this next phase, strong internal communication will be essential to keeping teams focused, connected, and moving in the same direction.
