title: Product Manager - Juno
descriptionHtml:
At Joko, our mission is to we help consumers save time and money when shopping online or in-store.

Founded in Paris, Joko is a tech company and certified B Corp with over 120 talents across Paris, Barcelona, and New York (and beyond). More than 7 million users already save money every day at 10,000+ merchants with Joko.

From cashback and automatic coupons to price alerts, we've kept expanding our products to make shopping smarter. Today, Joko is an AI shopping app: with Juno, our shopping assistant, users can find the right product at the best price in only a few seconds, with recommendations that get sharper the more they use it.

Having reached profitability in our core market, we’re now scaling globally, with a strong focus on the US.

It’s still day 1, come build the future of shopping with us!

📱 Our Product Team

Led by Fabien, our VP Product, Joko's Product team groups the passionate individuals behind our users' delight! From brainstorming to development to launch, the Product team's main mission is to turn ideas into reality by working hand-in-hand with the Engineering, Design, and Business teams.

Joko is organized into four product tribes, each owning a key dimension of the company's value:

  • Business lines owns the current core value proposition, covering online shopping, in-store experiences, and gift cards, each run as a dedicated team.

  • Scale focuses on growing and amplifying this value through growth, international expansion, and shared core user experiences across the app.

  • Juno builds the next value proposition: an AI shopping assistant that finds the right product at the best price in seconds, backed by a universal catalog of what merchants actually sell.

  • AI Platform helps Joko become a state-of-the-art AI company from the inside, owning the internal agent infrastructure, automation layer, internal tools, infrastructure, compliance, security and operational scalability.

🤖 The Engine task force

Juno is Joko's most ambitious bet: becoming the front door to shopping. An AI assistant that understands what someone is genuinely looking for, searches thousands of merchants at once, and gets them to the right decision in seconds rather than hours — the reflex people reach for before they buy anything.

The Juno tribe is split into two task forces. Engine owns the assistant itself: the conversational experience users interact with, and the product logic that turns an intent into the right recommendation. Catalog owns the universal product catalog that powers it.

Engine is where Juno meets the user. It owns the conversation itself: how someone expresses a vague intent, how the assistant narrows it down, and how a recommendation is presented so that it is actually trusted. Nobody has settled what a great shopping conversation looks like, so there are no patterns to borrow and the answers have to be found by building and testing.

The task force is a small, autonomous team: a Product Manager who owns it, a Product Designer, and software engineers. This role is its first Product Manager, so the scope, the standards, and the way the team works are yours to define.

🎯 What you will do

As Product Manager for the Engine task force, you own it. That means the end-to-end user experience of Juno, from the conversational interface on mobile and web to the product logic behind the recommendations. You will report to Yosr, who leads the Juno tribe, and work day to day with a Product Designer, software engineers, and the Catalog task force.

  • Conversational product design: There is no market standard for what a great shopping conversation looks like. You will define it. That means testing a lot, iterating fast, and inventing interaction patterns for a surface that has none yet.

  • Designing with AI's limits in mind: A model-backed flow behaves differently from a deterministic one. You will design for hallucinations, unexpected outputs, and edge cases: what the fallback is, what the model gets fed, what the user sees when it goes wrong. This is a large part of the craft in this role.

  • Discovery, user testing & iteration: You will run user tests continuously, read real conversations, spot where the experience breaks, and turn that into the next iteration. You will own the rollout strategy and decide what ships to whom, when.

  • Roadmap & ownership: You will define the vision and roadmap for the assistant experience, prioritise against company priorities and technical reality, and own delivery from problem framing to launch.

  • Measurement: Evaluating an AI experience is a hard problem in itself. You will define what quality means for Juno, build the metrics that track it, and use them to drive decisions.

  • Competitive positioning: Generic assistants ship new shopping capabilities constantly. You will define what makes a specialised shopping assistant win.

👀 Who we're looking for

  • Experience: You have at least 2 to 3 years of experience as a Product Manager. We are flexible on seniority, but you need enough depth to bring real experience to a team that is being built.

  • AI product experience: You have shipped user-facing features powered by AI, on a product with a meaningful user base. You know what it takes to put a model in front of real users and keep the experience good.

  • UX & UI judgment: You have strong instincts on user experience and interface, and you have wrestled with the specific difficulty of designing an AI feature. This role is deeply user-facing, and this criterion carries the most weight.

  • Data fluency: You are comfortable defining metrics, instrumenting them, and evaluating outcomes with numbers. Every decision on this team is backed by data.

  • AI fluency: You are hands-on and genuinely curious about AI tools and how models behave. Juno is built on AI, so you will be in the product every day.

  • ML knowledge: A strong bonus. The engineers bring that depth already, so we weigh UX judgment on AI features more heavily than model internals.

  • 0-to-1 appetite: You want to build something that does not exist yet. Blank pages energise you.

  • Location: Based in France or Spain.

  • Languages: Fluent in English, both written and spoken. French is a plus, but it is optional.

  • Mindset: You have an entrepreneurial mindset, you like challenges, you welcome feedback and you love constantly learning and getting better.

💎 Our perks

(Some of the benefits listed below are available to full-time positions only)

At Joko, we believe that flexibility and trust are essential. Our work environment reflects this through:

  • Flexible remote : If you live in Paris, you can choose to work from our office or from home with no constraints. If you live elsewhere, we can provide access to a coworking space and a coworking budget.

  • Work from anywhere : Want to spend a month in Italy while working? You can work from most countries in the world for up to 3 months per year.

On top of that, we offer plenty of perks:

  • 💸 Top-market compensation

  • 📈 Equity for everyone with the chance to own a piece of what you build

  • 🤖 Half-day each week dedicated to leveling up with AI by exploring new tools, iterating hard, and sharpening your skills

  • 🌴 Yearly offsite in amazing locations and budget for team-building events & monthly in-person gatherings

  • 💪 Contribution to your ClassPass subscription

  • 🍼 8-week leave paid 100% for the second parent

  • …and much more, check the full list here!

🤝 Our hiring process

  1. Intro call: Quick screening with the Hiring Manager or the Talent team.

  2. Step 1 – Team interview (45 min): Conversation with two Joko team members (could include the Hiring Manager, people from the team you’d join, or colleagues from other teams).

  3. Step 2 – Role-specific assessments

    • For non-engineering roles: A take-home case study followed by a 45-min interview. We assess both your output and how you think in real time. The exercise will be relevant to your role (e.g. analysis, strategy, or process design).

    • For engineering roles: A 90-min live technical interview on CoderPad covering code understanding, review, system design, and product thinking (with AI serving as a collaboration tool).

  4. Step 3 – Leadership interview (45 min): Conversation with a SteerCo member and a Founder.

  5. References: Up to 3 calls with former colleagues or managers.

☕ You may also be invited for coffee with team members to get a feel for our culture.

Compensation: €64K – €104K • Offers Equity

title: Product Manager
descriptionHtml:
Product Manager, Lead to Cash

Location: London, onsite 5 days a week

Retire The ERP.

Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our Smart Financial Platform gives modern, global companies superpowers: automated accounting, real-time reporting, and financial flows that move at the speed of the business.

We build with our customers, ship fast, and obsess over craft. In a short time, Light has gone from idea to the operating core for leading companies like Lovable, Legora, and Keyshot. We’re an early team defining a new software category. If you’re excited to modernise how the world runs money, one agentic workflow at a time, you’re in the right place.

Backed by world-class investors and advised by industry titans, we’re building category-defining products with the freedom to ship ambitiously and own outcomes. Come help us make Light the global default for next-gen finance.

About The Role

This is a hands-on product role reporting to the VP of Product Development. You’ll own Lead to Cash: everything between a signed deal and cash in the bank. That covers contracts, billing and invoicing, revenue recognition, payments, and credit control. You’ll set the roadmap for the area with the VP, and your discovery and judgement decide what actually ships.

In Lead to Cash, the ledger has to keep up with whatever commercial terms each customer signs. A contract changes mid-term, and the invoices, deferred revenue and reporting all have to follow. A parent company wants one bill for a dozen subsidiaries. A customer’s Stripe setup doesn’t match how they actually sell. Every customer bills a little differently, and the product has to absorb those differences without turning into a pile of one-offs. You work out which problems are patterns worth building for and which aren’t, and you say so.

Your stakeholders are engineers, designers, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Implementation, and the Financial Controllers, Finance Directors and CFOs who run their revenue on Light. Most of them are senior, technical and short of time. They expect you to keep up, and to be honest with them when a request would cost more than it’s worth.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the Lead to Cash roadmap and its delivery, from discovery to go-live, and the metrics that show whether it’s working for customers

  • Turn contract terms, pricing models and revenue recognition rules into product requirements engineers can build from

  • Decide which customer requests become product and which don’t, and bring a clear recommendation to the VP of Product Development when the call is a big one

  • Lead discovery with finance teams: sit with them through a billing run or a month-end close and find what’s slow, manual or wrong

  • Work with Sales and Solutions Engineering on what gets promised to customers, before it’s promised

  • Sequence delivery with Engineering and Design without cutting the corners that matter in finance

  • Own the integrations that feed Lead to Cash, such as CRMs and payment providers, with clear scope for each

  • Spot a release going off-track before it slips, and escalate or intervene early

  • Enable the teams downstream of you (Sales, SE, Implementation, Support) to sell, set up and support every Lead to Cash feature from day one

  • Shape how AI agents run billing and collections work, inside policies that finance teams set and can audit

Experience & Qualifications*

We’re looking for someone with around 4–8 years in product (or equivalent experience), who brings:

  • You ship product, not slideware. You’ve owned real features that real users depend on. You measure yourself by what went live and what it changed, not by the roadmap you maintained. This is the non-negotiable.

  • You turn accounting rules into product. You can read IFRS 15 or ASC 606, a customer’s master services agreement, or a messy pricing sheet and work out what the product has to do. You know why a mid-term upgrade, a backdated discount or an early termination breaks a simple billing model, and you design for it before a customer finds it.

  • You know revenue. You understand order-to-cash in practice: contracts, billing schedules, deferred and recognised revenue, credit notes, dunning, and matching cash against invoices. You can talk confidently with a Controller about how revenue should land in the books. An accounting qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CPA or local equivalent) is a strong plus, and so is time spent running billing or revenue operations yourself.

  • You can say no, explain why, and keep the relationship intact. Lead to Cash attracts customer-specific requests, and many arrive already promised. You can tell a pattern from a one-off, explain the cost of each to Sales and to customers, and turn the patterns into product that serves the next customer as well as this one.

  • You’re AI-native. You’ve changed the way you work because of AI tooling, not just added it to your workflow. You use it to read contracts and pricing models, prototype, draft specs and pressure-test your own thinking, and you have an instinct for where it helps, where it misleads, and how to use it without losing ownership of the outcome.

  • You own discovery. You talk to customers directly and often: their finance teams, the people who run their billing, and our own Sales and Implementation teams who set them up. You can tell the difference between what a customer asks for and the problem underneath it, and you turn that into the smallest thing worth building next.

  • You deliver through other people. You’ve shipped through Product, Engineering, Design and Sales without formal authority over any of them. You build trust with senior finance stakeholders through clear communication and consistent delivery.

  • Fluent English; additional European languages a plus.

*If the core of the role sounds compelling but you don’t tick every box, we’d still love for you to reach out and convince us you’re the right person.

Bonus Points

  • Experience building billing, subscription or revenue recognition products, or running billing at a SaaS company

  • Familiarity with billing and payment platforms such as Stripe, Chargebee or Zuora, and CRMs such as HubSpot or Salesforce

  • Experience in fintech or systems where data integrity is non-negotiable

  • Experience with usage-based, tiered or hybrid pricing models

  • Background in high-growth startups where everything was still being figured out

  • Familiarity with multi-currency, multi-entity billing and e-invoicing mandates (e.g. Peppol, Italy’s SDI)

You’ll Probably Struggle Here If

  • You need a finished spec handed to you. Here the “requirement” is often a contract clause or a pricing sheet nobody has turned into product yet.

  • You need a PMO, a mature methodology or a big delivery org around you to operate. This is a startup environment, and ownership and a self-starter nature are key.

  • You treat every customer request as a commitment. The job is deciding which ones become product.

  • You find it hard to say no to a customer or colleague, even when it’s the right call.

  • You haven’t yet changed how you work because of AI. We go all in on AI at Light and want people who share that.

Our Tech Stack

We build on AWS, with a Kotlin backend, a React frontend, and infrastructure managed in Terraform. It’s a real production system that global finance teams depend on every day.

You won’t be writing the code, but you’ll live alongside it. You do need to be comfortable in this kind of environment: real scale, real customers, real stakes.

The Good Stuff

In addition to being part of a great team and working in a fun and innovative environment, we offer:

💸 A competitive salary and potential stock options.
🏝 A generous paid annual leave package, plus UK public holidays.
🥳 Regular socials and two company offsites a year. The last 2 were in Tuscany & Provence!
🚀 A huge opportunity for career growth as you help shape a market-defining product.

Light is an equal opportunity employer.

The Famous Last Words

Working at Light means you’re embarking on an exciting journey to reshape the future of multinational financial operations. Our cheat code is that we’ve built something like this before, and now we’re doing it again, only better. Our goal is to make global finance effortless and empower companies to make informed decisions.

Join the rocket ship while it’s taking off 🚀

title: Product Marketing & Growth Intern (H/F)
descriptionHtml:
About Pysae

Pysae is a French SaaS company building real-time fleet supervision (AVM / SAEIV) and workforce management software for public transport operators. Bus networks, coach operators and transport authorities in France and across Europe rely on our platform every day to run their services, inform passengers and manage their drivers. We are a team of around 40 people based in Rennes, Paris and Italy, and we are expanding fast internationally.

Pysae has grown from a set of products into a full platform. We now need someone to help tell that story, put it in front of the right people, and turn it into growth.

The internship

Reporting to our Chief Revenue Officer (CRO), you will work on product marketing and growth: generating demand through the product itself and by showcasing the value of the Pysae platform. You will be given real responsibilities from day one, not side tasks.

This is an international role. You will work on France, Italy and our new markets across Europe and beyond, with sales teams and customers in several countries and languages.

This is not a classic marketing internship. Our market (public transport operators and authorities) has long been sold to in the same way: tenders, trade shows and long sales cycles. We want to break that pattern. Your mission is to help us invent, test and deploy new ways of selling and growing, using the product, content, data and AI as levers. You will have a blank page, direct access to the CRO and the founders, and the freedom to try things that have never been done in our industry.

It is a very exciting internship, and a demanding one: you will need to come up with ideas, prove quickly whether they work, drop what doesn't and scale what does.

Your missions

Invent new sales & growth methods

  • Imagine new ways to reach, engage and convert transport operators and authorities, beyond the traditional tender-driven playbook

  • Design and run fast experiments (new channels, formats, offers, outreach sequences, product-led motions), measure the results and turn the winners into repeatable playbooks for the sales team

  • Bring fresh ideas from other industries and from the latest AI and growth practices, and adapt them to our market

Product marketing & positioning

  • Help sharpen the positioning and messaging of the Pysae platform and its modules for each segment (urban networks, interurban and school transport, on-demand transport, rail) and each country

  • Turn product releases into launches: release notes, feature pages, demo videos, customer-facing announcements

  • Build sales enablement material with the sales team, in French and English: pitch decks, one-pagers, case studies, battlecards, ROI arguments

International growth

  • Support our expansion into new countries: market-entry campaigns, localised messaging and content, lead generation for our international sales team

  • Contribute to product-led growth initiatives: onboarding, in-app messaging, feature adoption, upsell and cross-sell across our customer base

  • Create and run campaigns (LinkedIn, email, webinars, international trade shows, content) that generate qualified pipeline for the sales team

  • Produce creative content that showcases the platform and our customers: case studies, articles, videos, social posts

  • Track and report on what works (traffic, leads, conversion, adoption) and double down on it

AI & automation

  • Use AI tools intensively to create and translate content, personalise outreach, analyse data and run campaigns at scale

  • Automate as many marketing and sales workflows as possible (CRM, emailing, reporting, content production), and document them so they keep running after your internship

Practical details

  • Contract: 6-month internship (with an internship agreement from your school)

  • Location: Paris, Rennes or Florence

  • Languages: French and English required

  • Reports to: Chief Revenue Officer

  • Start date: as soon as possible


  • Fluent French and English (both required), written and spoken; Italian or another European language is a plus

  • Currently enrolled in a business or marketing school, ideally in the final year of a Master's programme, and able to sign a 6-month internship agreement

  • A previous internship or project in marketing, growth or digital marketing is a plus, ideally in B2B SaaS and/or in an international environment

  • A truly creative mindset: you love inventing new approaches, you are not afraid of a blank page, and you would rather test a bold idea than copy a playbook

  • An entrepreneurial, hands-on attitude: you turn ideas into experiments quickly, learn from failures and keep going

  • An international mindset: you enjoy working across countries and cultures, and adapting your message to each market

  • A strong AI user: you already use tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Notion AI, Make/Zapier or similar to work faster, and you are curious about what comes next

  • Data-driven: you measure, test and iterate

  • Autonomous, organised and comfortable with ambiguity in a fast-moving scale-up

  • An interest in mobility, public transport or tech for the public good is a plus

title: Production Engineer, Network
descriptionHtml:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Production Engineering Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Turn every network fault from a mystery into a closed ticket. Link diagnostics across router to router and NIC to router paths, remote command execution across the fleet, and repair visualization that shows what's broken and why, because at 10s of GW scale debugging has to be systematic, not artisanal.

  • Build the network repair pipeline that runs itself. Automated fault detection through RMA initiation, ticket integration, transceiver lifecycle tracking, and return to service, across DC fabric, edge, and host to network layers, because a new site comes online every six months and manual repair doesn't keep up.

  • Build the network monitoring platform for a fleet that never stops growing. Alerting lifecycle and health dashboards for infrastructure spanning multiple hyperscale sites today and 10s of GW next year. It doesn't exist yet. We're building it.

Role Scope

  • Carry the on-call pager for the network fleet and run repair end to end: diagnose the fault, execute the fix or drive the RMA, and return the link to service across DC fabric, edge, and host to network layers.

  • Write Python and Go tooling that replaces manual diagnosis, including link tests, remote command execution across the fleet, and repair visualization that shows what's broken and why, so faults resolve in minutes, not hours.

  • Automate the repair pipeline from fault detection through RMA initiation, ticket integration, transceiver and optics tracking, and return to service, so a failure at any site follows the same path without manual handoffs.

  • Maintain the realtime monitoring and alerting that gives every on-call engineer a true picture of network health across all sites, and keep it accurate as new sites and hardware roll in.

  • Validate new sites and hardware into production by running the qualification tests that confirm a network is healthy before it carries traffic.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've carried a pager for a production network and can walk into an outage, find the fault, fix it or drive the RMA, and write the postmortem without someone walking you through it.

  • You've written Python or Go scripts that replaced a manual, repetitive network task, from link diagnostics to config pushes to fleet-wide command execution.

  • You understand how a transceiver fault, a misconfigured route, and a power event each show up differently in the data, and you can tell them apart from the signals alone.

  • You've worked hands-on with link diagnostics, optics, and network monitoring protocols such as gNMI, gRPC, NETCONF, and SONiC, and you're comfortable at the CLI on switches and routers across a fleet.

  • You treat toil as a bug. If a repair step means SSHing into ten boxes by hand, you script it once and never do it by hand again.

  • You reach real competence in an unfamiliar part of the stack fast, and you document what you learn so the next on-call engineer doesn't start from zero.

  • Bonus: RMA and repair lifecycle automation. Large-scale datacenter fabric (BGP, ECMP, spine-leaf). Out-of-band network management. Fluency with AI coding tools such as Claude Code or Cursor to move faster on scripts and tooling.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

title: Projektleiter:in Elektrotechnik
descriptionHtml:
Bringe Technik in große Bauwerke im Stahlwasserbau!

Hinter beeindruckenden Objekte wie Schleusen, Wehranlagen oder Schiffshebewerken steckt weit mehr als nur Stahl und Beton – erst die Elektrotechnik macht sie funktional. Genau hier kommst du ins Spiel.

Als Projektleiter im Bereich Elektrotechnik gestaltest du bei uns komplexe Anlagen im Stahlwasserbau und bringst innovative Technik in wasserbauliche Anlagen. Von der ersten Planung über technische Berechnungen bis hin zur finalen Umsetzung begleitest du Projekte, die wirklich etwas bewegen – im wahrsten Sinne des Wortes.

Wenn du Lust hast, Elektrotechnik mit spannenden Infrastrukturprojekten zu verbinden und gemeinsam mit einem erfahrenen Team nachhaltige Lösungen zu entwickeln, dann freuen wir uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.

Aufgaben

Darauf kannst du dich bei uns freuen

  • Planung anspruchsvoller Anlagen
    Du planst und konstruierst elektrische Anlagen im Stahlwasserbau – etwa für Schleusen, Wehranlagen oder Schiffshebewerke – und begleitest die Projekte von der ersten Idee bis zur Umsetzung.
  • Technische Berechnungen und Auslegung
    Du dimensionierst Energienetze und sorgst durch fundierte Berechnungen dafür, dass Anlagen effizient, sicher und zuverlässig funktionieren.
  • Steuerungs- und Beleuchtungstechnik
    Von der Planung moderner Steuerungstechnik bis hin zu detaillierten Beleuchtungsberechnungen bringst du deine elektrotechnische Expertise in verschiedene Bereiche der Anlagenplanung ein.
  • Planung und Dokumentation
    Du erstellst Leistungsbeschreibungen und Leistungsverzeichnisse als Grundlage für die Umsetzung der Projekte und sorgst für eine vollständige und nachvollziehbare technische Dokumentation.
  • Technische Zeichnungen und Planung
    Du erstellst, bearbeitest und optimierst technische Zeichnungen sowie Pläne, Grundrisse, Schnitte und Ansichten. Dabei führst du auch Zeichnungskonvertierungen und Anpassungen bestehender Unterlagen durch.
  • Präzise Planung bis ins Detail
    Mit deiner strukturierten Arbeitsweise stellst du sicher, dass alle Planungsunterlagen aktuell, vollständig und technisch sauber ausgearbeitet sind.

Qualifikation

Mit diesem Profil bist du die ideale Ergänzung für unser Team

  • Du hast ein Studium der Elektrotechnik erfolgreich abgeschlossen oder verfügst über eine vergleichbare Qualifikation.
  • Idealerweise hast du bereits erste Erfahrung im Planungsumfeld technischer Anlagen gesammelt und bringst Interesse an anspruchsvollen Infrastrukturprojekten mit.
    Erfahrung im Stahlwasserbau ist kein Muss – wichtiger ist uns deine Neugier auf Technik, die große Wassermengen bewegt und steuert.
  • Normen, Richtlinien und technische Regelwerke schrecken dich nicht ab – im Gegenteil: Du arbeitest gerne damit und behältst auch im Regelwerksdschungel den Überblick.
  • Du arbeitest strukturiert, selbstständig und lösungsorientiert und behältst auch bei komplexen Aufgaben den Überblick. Gleichzeitig bist du ein Teamplayer, der gerne gemeinsam mit Kollegen und Projektbeteiligten an optimalen Lösungen arbeitet.
  • Ein sicherer Umgang mit den gängigen Office-Anwendungen rundet dein Profil ab.

Benefits

Das macht uns besonders

Wir sind überzeugt: Ein guter Arbeitsplatz besteht nicht nur aus spannenden Aufgaben, sondern vor allem aus einem starken Team und einem Umfeld, in dem man sich wohlfühlt.

  • Ein Team, das zusammenhält
    Bei uns arbeitest du in einem motivierten und erfahrenen Team, das sich gegenseitig unterstützt. Offene Kommunikation, gegenseitiger Respekt und ein unkompliziertes Miteinander gehören für uns ganz selbstverständlich dazu.
  • Projekte, die wirklich etwas bewegen
    Unsere Projekte im Stahlwasserbau sind technisch anspruchsvoll und alles andere als alltäglich. Dadurch erwarten dich abwechslungsreiche Aufgaben, bei denen du dein Fachwissen einbringen und weiterentwickeln kannst.
  • Flache Hierarchien, schnelle Entscheidungen
    Dank flacher Hierarchien und kurzer Entscheidungswege können Ideen schnell umgesetzt werden. Deine Vorschläge finden bei uns immer ein offenes Ohr.
  • Arbeiten in moderner Umgebung
    Helle Büroräume, moderne Ausstattung und Parkplätze direkt vor der Tür sorgen für einen angenehmen und unkomplizierten Arbeitsalltag.
  • Arbeiten, wie es zu deinem Leben passt

title: Recruiter (Temporary Contract)
descriptionHtml:
This is a temporary role, running from now until around February 2027. It is not a permanent position.

Location: London (next to East Croydon Station)

Hybrid: 2 days in the office - negotiable

Contract: Temporary, from now until around February 2027

Reports to: Head of Talent Acquisition (Joe Morrison)

Compensation: £30,000 to £35,000 pro rata, depending on experience

Target start: ASAP

About Us

Hozah is a tech-led, award-winning company driving change in the parking industry and reimagining urban mobility. Our mission is simple but powerful: to transform parking into a seamless, automated experience, paving the way for smarter, more sustainable cities.

With recent recognition as PayTech Company of the Year, a place among Deloitte's Top 50 Fastest Growing Tech Companies in the UK, and significant VC/PE investment, we're one of the fastest scaling companies in the country.

Role Overview

We have a busy few months ahead, with 20 to 30 hires to make before the spring. Many of them sit in our commercial and go-to-market teams, particularly junior sales, alongside site engineering and other junior roles. The difference between a good hire and a missed one is often how quickly a strong applicant gets a call.

You will be the first voice candidates hear from Hozah. Working alongside our Head of Talent Acquisition, you'll run first-round interviews at volume, by phone or video, giving every candidate a clear, compelling picture of Hozah and the role, and keeping every application moving.

After each call you'll make a recommendation, and our Head of Talent Acquisition will decide who progresses. Success in this role is simple to measure: a high, consistent volume of first interviews each week, and a high proportion of the people you recommend going on to a second interview. We want hiring managers to trust that anyone you put forward is worth their time.

You'll also support our sourcing using Metaview, and lend a hand with onboarding as new starters join.

This is a temporary contract running from now until around February 2027, and the scope can flex for the right person.

Key Responsibilities

  • Run a high, consistent volume of first-round interviews each week, particularly for commercial and go-to-market roles such as junior sales, as well as site engineering and other junior roles.

  • Represent Hozah brilliantly on every call: explain who we are, what the role involves and why it's worth joining, so strong candidates leave wanting to take the next step.

  • Write clear, structured notes after every call and make a recommendation, so our Head of Talent Acquisition can make fast progression decisions. A high proportion of the people you recommend should reach a second interview.

  • Keep the application inbox moving, booking calls promptly so no candidate waits long to hear from us, and keep the ATS accurate and up to date.

  • Source candidates directly using Metaview, so your call diary stays full when applications are thin.

  • Make sure every candidate, including those who don't progress, has a responsive and professional experience that represents Hozah well.

  • Support onboarding for new starters, such as preparing paperwork and coordinating first-day logistics, so that hires land smoothly.

Who we're looking for

  • An excellent speaker who presents confidently and persuasively, on the phone and on video. You can bring a company and a role to life in a few minutes.

  • Recruitment or resourcing experience, in-house or agency, with a track record of running high volumes of candidate calls.

  • Highly desirable: experience with commercial and go-to-market roles, such as sales, business development or account management, ideally in B2B tech or another high-growth environment.

  • Comfortable working to numbers. You know your calls per week and how many of the people you put forward reach a next stage, and you can tell us yours.

  • Highly organised, with tidy notes, a well-kept pipeline and reliable follow-up.

  • Warm, professional and at ease talking to people at every level.

  • Confident sourcing candidates directly, not just working from applications. Experience with an ATS and AI recruiting tools, ideally Metaview, would be an advantage.

  • Available to start soon and to commit to a temporary contract until around February 2027.

What We Offer

  • Hybrid working: 2 days in the office preferred, negotiable.

  • A chance to make a real difference during a key growth period for Hozah.

  • Hands-on experience with a modern recruitment tech stack.

  • A friendly, high-performing team.

  • A fully refurbished, modern office right next to East Croydon Station, with a fully stocked kitchen offering free breakfast, lunch and drinks!

Compensation: £30K – £35K • Pro rata for a temporary contract until around Feb 2027

title: Regional Director of Sales
descriptionHtml:
About the Role at RobCo

RobCo is building the category of Autonomous Industrial Robotics and we're doing it fast. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works.

 

As our Regional Director of Enterprise Sales, you act as the primary catalyst for RobCo's enterprise growth across the German market, driving large-scale industrial adoption of our Autonomous Manufacturing Platform. You will lead high-impact sales strategies, build strategic relationships with executive stakeholders in key industrial sectors, and scale our enterprise footprint from the ground up.

Your Responsibilities

  • Drive Regional Revenue: Lead and execute the German enterprise sales strategy to achieve and exceed ambitious revenue and market-penetration targets.

  • Build Executive Relationships: Target, engage, and secure long-term partnerships with C-level executives and key decision-makers across mid-market and large-scale manufacturing and industrial enterprises.

  • Champion Technical Solutions: Direct complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise sales cycles by clearly communicating the strategic, financial, and technical ROI of RobCo's modular robotics and physical AI solutions.

  • Scale Enterprise Footprint: Identify and unlock new market verticals and geographic opportunities across the DACH region to continually expand the sales pipeline.

  • Partner Cross-Functionally: Collaborate closely with Solution Engineering and Product teams to align client requirements with product capabilities and deliver seamless rollouts.

  • Forecast with Accuracy: Maintain meticulous pipeline hygiene, actionable sales reporting, and highly accurate quarterly/annual revenue forecasts in Salesforce.

  • Represent the Brand: Position RobCo as the premier AI-driven automation provider through representation at key industry events, panel discussions, and executive roundtables.

  • Team Leadership & Enablement: Lead, mentor, and coach a high-performing team of Senior Account Executives, driving quota attainment, pipeline growth, and continuous performance management.

xpate also wants to become AI-native. Guardrails go around the core – the data layer and financial data – so it can’t be lost, rewritten or broken. Everything else runs through an agentic harness on top, so non-engineering teams can build their own tools by prompting agents.

title: Senior AI Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Codat

Codat is an advisory intelligence solution purpose-built for modern commercial banking. Through rich, specialized data, forward-looking insights, and integrated workflows, Codat empowers banking teams to deepen their relationships, grow their revenue, and simplify their day-to-day work.

Founded in 2017 and backed by JPMorgan, PayPal, Amex, Plaid, and Shopify, Codat has successfully powered over 350,000 connections to business customers’ financial systems — and is trusted by industry leaders to turn scattered information into actionable, strategic advantages in real time, every time.

The Role

Some of the biggest commercial banks in the world already work with us. Their relationship managers would rather spend time with clients than dig through the books to find out what's changed. We're building this for them.

We're building the Advisory Intelligence Platform. It puts Codat's client intelligence inside the assistant a banker already uses, starting with Microsoft Copilot. A banker can ask it anything about a client and get an answer from that client's actual books. If they don't ask, it tells them anyway when something important changes, and suggests what to do.

It's a senior role and a hands-on one. Bankers make real decisions based on what the assistant says, so impressing people in a demo isn't enough. It has to be right. Codat is AI-first, not AI bolted onto SaaS, and we work that way ourselves, with agents handling the repetitive work so engineers can focus on the hard problems. You'll build what you design and look after it once it's live, and you'll have a real say in where we take it.

What You'll Work On

  • The reasoning layer. What goes into the model's context, which tools it calls, and when it should break a question into steps. Every number it gives has to trace back to a source, and it needs to know when to say it doesn't know. That last part is harder than it sounds.

  • Evals. You'll build the eval sets and harness, and do the analysis that tells us whether a change made the assistant better or just different. When a banker corrects an answer, that correction becomes a new test case.

  • Model choice and token economics. Which model should handle which job, and what that costs us per answer. Caching or a smaller model is often enough. For some questions a banker needs the strongest model available, and that's worth paying for.

  • The semantic and signal layers. You'll work on both with the data engineers. That means the definitions the model is allowed to use, and the signals that spot when something changes for a client. How the model uses them is down to you.

  • The agents and MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers behind the assistant. This covers the tools the assistant can call, including the ones that will eventually let it draft that email. You'll work out how they break, and add the tracing we need to see what happened inside an answer.

  • Classical modelling where it beats an LLM. Anomaly detection, peer benchmarks, classifiers. Sometimes the best answer is a simple statistical model, not an LLM.

You'll Probably Have

  • Shipped LLM features that people actually used, and been the person they came to when something broke. You've designed how a model works with tools or structured data, and there are things you'd do differently now.

  • Built evals for your own work, and probably had one mislead you. We'd like to hear what you changed.

  • A feel for numbers, whether that comes from a quantitative degree or from your work. You want the denominator before you believe a percentage, and you notice when a headline figure is really about the mix of the data.

  • Opinions about models that come from using them. You've chosen between models on how well they did and what they cost, and you know when a classical model would do a better job.

  • Good engineering habits in Python or another general-purpose language. That means tested, modular services rather than notebooks. Strong SQL as well, and some experience with CI/CD, Docker, cloud (we're on Azure) and tracing for LLM systems.

  • Led work without having the title. People followed an approach you set because you made the case with evidence, and you can explain the trade-offs to someone who isn't technical.

  • AI as part of how you work, for research and prototyping as well as code.

  • Useful, not essential: fintech, lending or accounting; Spark or Databricks; semantic layers or metric views; fine-tuning.

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. We're more interested in what you've built and how you knew it worked than in a perfect match.

How We Work

We're a small team with plenty to do. Things move fast: we'd rather ship something useful and improve it than polish it in private. What you build is yours from start to finish.

There's no return-to-office mandate, and you can work hybrid or fully remote. We trust you to be around when the team needs you and to deliver what you said you would. What we don't want is anyone staying online late to prove a point.

Compensation: £98K – £115K • Offers Equity

descriptionHtml:
At Luscii, we're creating space for care by developing and improving digital healthcare applications that make a real difference in people's lives through several applications. From Luscii Thuismeten, which helps healthcare professionals monitor patients remotely, to OMRON Connect, connecting millions of people with their health data through OMRON devices, and other applications that expand the possibilities of digital healthcare.

Together with healthcare professionals and partners around the world, we're working towards a future where people receive the right care in the right place. As our Senior Cloud Engineer, you'll help shape and modernise the cloud infrastructure behind these applications, building a reliable, scalable and future-proof foundation for millions of users worldwide.

Our applications have different histories, architectures and technical challenges. OMRON Connect, for example, runs on an AWS backend serving several million monthly active users. Parts of its infrastructure still carry legacy, including manual processes, scattered knowledge, inconsistent observability and release processes that make changes slower and riskier than they should be.

We're working towards a more consistent engineering foundation across our applications. Think Infrastructure as Code, cloud-native and event-driven architecture where it adds value, safe continuous deployment and observability by default. We're bringing more senior engineering expertise in-house to turn that ambition into concrete technical decisions, shared standards and a roadmap our teams can own. And that's where you come in 😉

Your role

You will work across our engineering teams, helping shape the cloud infrastructure behind our digital healthcare applications. Your focus will be on making the right architectural decisions, modernising existing platforms and enabling teams to independently build, maintain and improve their systems.

This isn't a greenfield architecture exercise. You will be improving live healthcare platforms while balancing technical improvements with product delivery, security, regulatory requirements and the realities of working with stakeholders across different countries, including the Netherlands and Japan.

What you will be doing, among others:

  • Own and evolve the Cloud & Backend roadmap, translating the engineering vision into clear priorities, trade-offs and next steps.

  • Drive cross-team architecture decisions to a close, making sure decisions are transparent, documented and followed through.

  • Establish shared technical standards and guardrails that allow teams to work autonomously without creating unnecessary dependencies.

  • Work hands-on with engineers on AWS and Terraform, reviewing designs and pull requests and challenging technical choices where needed.

  • Coach and pair with engineers, helping knowledge spread across teams and supporting the growth of seniority and ownership.

  • Work with product owners, QA, engineering leadership and colleagues in Japan to balance technical direction with product, regulatory, security and cost considerations.

  • Help move the platform towards automated infrastructure, safer deployments and stronger observability without relying on a big-bang rewrite.

The responsibilities outlined above reflect how we currently envision this role. As we continue to grow and evolve, the scope and focus of the position may naturally change, influenced by your own ideas and insights. The way we work is built around the belief that everyone's input matters. If you see opportunities to improve the way we do things, or believe a process could be designed differently to achieve a better outcome, we encourage you to bring those ideas forward. Discuss them with your teammates, challenge the status quo, and help shape how we move forward together.

Why Luscii?

Read more about working at Luscii / OMRON and how we work as a team. Together, we are working on a mission to create space for care. Freedom, autonomy and ownership are of great importance in this. You are responsible for your own results and work according to the principles of Holacracy. Luscii is part of OMRON DH; together we built for the long term. To work on making healthcare better.

Most important benefits

  • Salary: An annual maximum remuneration of approximately € 85.000 gross per year is estimated for this position (based on 32 hours per week – that’s full-time at Luscii), depending on the interviews, your experience, background and knowledge.

  • Remote-first: Work from anywhere in The Netherlands. We stay connected through monthly in-person team days called Assemblii.

  • Flexible setup: Create your own ideal workspace. Whatever works best for you - we’ve got you covered here. We do work from Mondays to Thursdays, as 32 hours per week is fulltime.

The ideal candidate…

… probably doesn't exist, but if you can tick most of the checkboxes below, please apply! We are looking for someone who enjoys taking ownership of complex technical challenges, makes pragmatic engineering decisions, and is excited about helping others succeed along the way.

You know when to step up, when to involve colleagues and when to move forward decisively. Working independently does not mean working in isolation for you. You feel at ease being both a self-starter and a committed team player, contributing to shared goals while taking responsibility for your own domain. You value open communication, transparency, and mutual trust.

  • You have at least 5+ years of experience in cloud/backend engineering and multiple years of hands-on experience with AWS and Terraform (Infrastructure as Code).

  • You are comfortable reviewing designs and pull requests. Experience with serverless and event-driven architectures is very valuable. All combined with experience in serverless AWS, Node.js/TypeScript tech stacks.

  • You actively coach, pair, review and share knowledge, with a focus on building ownership and seniority across the teams around you.

  • You understand what matters: the importance of making pragmatic technical choices within clear security, compliance and regulatory boundaries.

  • You are open to working in a Holacratic organization and curious about our way of organizing work, roles, and responsibilities;

  • English is our primary language for all internal communication at Luscii, so you're fluent in that language.

Interested? Apply now!

Would you like more information? Feel free to contact our recruiter Björn Bogerd via

What does the recruitment process look like?

We organise three interviews for each vacancy. It is an extensive process, but we want to ensure that there is a good fit in regards to a potential collaboration, our culture and our way of working. All interviews are conducted online and the entire procedure is planned in advance to keep momentum.

title: Senior Customer Success Manager - DACH & North
descriptionHtml:
Amplitude is the leading AI analytics platform, helping over 5,200 customers—including Atlassian, Burger King, NBCUniversal, and Square—build better products and digital experiences. With powerful AI Agents embedded across our platform, teams can analyze, test, and optimize user experiences faster than ever. Ranked #1 across multiple categories in G2’s Winter 2026 Report, Amplitude is the best-in-class solution for product, data, and marketing teams. Learn more at amplitude.com.

As an organization, we deliver for our customers by living our values. We operate from a place of humility, take ownership of problems and successes, approach challenges with a growth mindset, and put our customers at the center of everything we do.

This role can be based in either Germany or the Netherlands

Own the outcome, not just the relationship.

Some of Europe’s biggest brands run on Amplitude. As a Senior Customer Success Manager, you make sure they get real results from it. You’ll own 15–20 Major Enterprise accounts across DACH, Benelux and the Nordics, and stay with each one from kickoff through renewal and expansion.

You’ll join an established, close-knit EMEA team where people build careers. Many of them have grown into bigger roles here, and you can too.

What you’ll do

  • Lead deployments end to end. Scope the work, build the plan, run kickoff, and coordinate internal and partner teams so every account hits its milestones.

  • Spot risk early and fix it. Use AI-powered health signals to catch adoption gaps and blockers before they affect timelines, renewals or results.

  • Grow adoption. Run hands-on working sessions, find new use cases, and show customers how new capabilities help them grow.

  • Tell the value story. Build success plans and executive business reviews that tie Amplitude usage to measurable business impact.

  • Drive revenue with your AE. Work together on renewals and expansion: coach champions, build the business case, and find the next opportunity.

  • Shape the product. Bring customer feedback back to Product so it influences what Amplitude builds next.

  • Raise the bar. Build playbooks, share what works, and help the team deliver at scale.

What sets you apart

  • Commercial instinct. You understand how each customer makes money and connect Amplitude to the results that matter to them.

  • Prescriptive by default. You know what good looks like, push back on bad implementation patterns, and hold customers to their own success criteria.

  • Diagnostic mind. You see problems coming and find creative ways around them.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity. You figure things out on your own and come to every conversation with a point of view.

  • AI-first. AI is already part of how you work, and you’re always testing better ways to use it.

What you bring

  • Proven Customer Success experience managing a portfolio of large Enterprise accounts

  • Experience with Enterprise deployments where change management and data governance were central

  • Clear commercial wins: customers you’ve retained and expanded

  • Strong communication and influencing skills, with exec presence

  • Solid project management skills and the drive to thrive in a fast-moving, independent role

Our values:

At Amplitude, our values guide how we show up for one another and for our customers:

  • Humility: We operate from a place of empathy and openness, seeking to understand many points of view.

  • Ownership: We take the initiative to solve problems that drive our shared company success.

  • Growth Mindset: We’re tenacious in the face of challenges and seek feedback in order to grow ourselves and others.

  • Customer Centricity: We put the customer at the center of everything we do and are deeply committed to their success.

We care about the well-being of our team: We offer competitive pay and benefits packages that reflect our commitment to the health and well-being of our Ampliteers.

Some of our benefit programs include:

  • Excellent ​M​edical, ​D​ental and ​V​ision insurance coverages, with 100% employer-paid premiums for employee Medical, ​Dental,​ ​​​​​​​​Vision on select plans

  • 401(k) retirement plan with an employer match of up to 1% of your eligible pay each pay period up to $2,000 annually

  • Flexible time off, ​p​aid holidays, and more

  • Generous stipends to spend on what matters most to you, whether that’s wellness (monthly), commuter transit/parking (monthly), learning and development (quarterly), new hire home office equipment, and much more

  • Excellent Parental benefits including​:​ 12 weeks of Paid Parental Leave, Carrot Fertility Benefits/Adoption/Surrogacy support, Back-up Child Care support

  • Mental health and wellness benefits including no cost employee access to Modern Health coaching & therapy sessions

  • Employee Stock Purchase Program​ (ESPP)

Other fun facts about Amplitude:

  • Our customers love us! They've said we're the #1 product analytics solution for 23 quarters in a row on G2.

  • We care a lot about product innovation. We've made significant investments in talent and infrastructure to build the most powerful AI analytics platform on the market.

  • We invest in our people. We offer mentorship programs, management training, and wellness initiatives.

  • We give back to our communities. We give every Ampliteer a charitable giving grant and paid volunteer time off.

  • We were founded in 2012, went public via a direct listing in September 2021, and are now trading under the ticker $AMPL.

  • We’re a global and fast-growing team! We have employees around the world and offices in San Francisco (HQ), New York, Vancouver, Amsterdam, London, Paris, Singapore, and Tokyo.

  • Our mascot is Data Monster, who loves to chow down on numbers, charts, and graphs. Nom nom.

By applying for this job, you acknowledge that Amplitude processes your personal data in accordance with the Amplitude Applicant Privacy Notice.

title: Senior Platform Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Attio is the CRM for agentic revenue. Designed for the most ambitious go-to-market teams, it gives companies the power to understand every customer, automate at scale, and build their go-to-market motion exactly as they need. We've raised $116M from some of the world's best investors: GV (Google Ventures), Redpoint, Balderton, Point Nine, and 01A.

We hire builders who thrive on complex technical challenges, hold themselves to a high bar, and genuinely care about delighting the people who use what they build. The team here brings sharp judgement, real craft, and the drive to do exceptional work. We're obsessed about the details and energized by the frontier.

If you want to do the best work of your career, this is the right place.


About the role

Our Engineering team tackles the toughest challenges, so our users never have to. Real-time infrastructure, AI-native architecture, and a frontend that feels effortless - all powered by a team that moves fast, thinks rigorously, and holds an exceptionally high bar for quality.

We're looking for Platform Engineers who treat the platform as a product, with every engineer at Attio as its customer. You'll own the infrastructure, tooling and pipelines that let the rest of engineering ship quickly and safely, and you'll be accountable for keeping all of it reliable, fast and cost-effective as we scale.

What you'll do

  • Build and evolve our platform infrastructure as code (Terraform, Kubernetes, GCP), so every environment is reproducible, version-controlled and auditable.

  • Own our CI/CD pipelines end-to-end, making builds, tests and deploys fast, reliable and secure for every engineer at Attio.

  • Own our observability stack - metrics, logging and distributed tracing - as the foundation of an exceptional reliability culture.

  • Define and hold SLOs for latency, availability and error rates, and manage capacity to stay comfortably inside them.

  • Lead incident response: triage and resolve complex production issues, then run blameless post-mortems and ship the fixes as code.

  • Partner with product engineering teams to remove manual toil and shorten the path from writing code to running it in production.

What you'll bring

  • Hands-on experience operating production systems with an SRE mindset: SLOs, error budgets, toil reduction and blameless post-mortems.

  • Excellent knowledge of modern cloud architectures (either GCP or AWS), including networking, IAM and managed services.

  • Demonstrable deep expertise with Docker and Kubernetes at scale, covering cluster design, networking, storage and security.

  • Proficiency in a modern language such as Typescript, Go, Python or Rust, and a track record of writing well-tested automation.

  • Experience owning mission-critical operational tooling, including centralised logging or APM (e.g. Datadog, Splunk).

  • Ability to communicate technical ideas to the wider team and influence how other engineers build and operate their services.

What we offer

  • Competitive salary of £105,000 to £125,000

  • Equity in an early-stage tech company on an incredible trajectory

  • 25 days holiday plus local public holidays

  • Apple hardware

  • Private medical insurance through AXA

  • Pension contribution through Hargreaves Lansdown

  • Enhanced family leave

  • Team off-site in fun places! (We've been to Barcelona, Lisbon, Malta, and Split so far)

Compensation: £105K – £125K • Offers Equity

title: Senior Product Marketing Manager (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
Fitness is the one industry where customers actually enjoy using the product. Help us tell that story well. At Sport Alliance, we're looking for someone who can bring clarity to our product portfolio and help us connect the right products with the right customers across different markets.

Every one of our products needs a clear reason to exist, a clear customer and a clear story. You’ll work alongside Product from the earliest sizing and segmentation conversations through to launch and adoption, so what we build is what the market wants and what Sales can sell.

As our Senior Product Marketing Manager, you'll shape product positioning, packaging, and go-to-market strategies, turning complex offerings into clear value propositions that Sales can confidently bring to customers.


Your position in our team

  • Tell one clear story per product. Own product positioning and messaging across our brands, creating clear, differentiated value propositions tailored to customer segments and markets.

  • Help decide what gets built, and why. Build market sizing and segmentation, and work with product so what we build meets customer needs and drives growth.

  • Shape packaging. Shape product packaging, working closely with Product, Pricing and Finance.

  • Launch things properly. Own go-to-market for key launches, from sizing and planning through to enablement. Join early, before the build, so the commercial view shapes the product from day one. Build a repeatable launch process that makes every launch smoother than the last.

  • Show what worked. Track adoption and conversion of new features and modules against the uplift we forecast. Where we hit it, find ways to do more. Where we didn't, learn why and feed it back into strategy. Your measures: product attachment, expansion MRR, win rate by segment and average deal value by product.

  • Stay close to customers and competitors. Talk to customers directly, run buyer research and win/loss, and own our ICPs. Build competitive intelligence as a living asset, with an AI agent doing the heavy lifting.

  • Equip Sales to win. Own the sales-facing narrative and build the tools: pitch narratives, battlecards, ROI calculators, case studies. Then see which ones get used and which ones move deals. Enable the sales team to tell the right story, and track whether they get used.

  • Build it, don't brief it. Use AI to speed up research and prototype pages, calculators and demos yourself. Hand the best ones to the agency or web team to scale.


    • Your profile

  • 6+ years of experience in Product Marketing, Product Management or a commercially focused product role within B2B SaaS.

  • Proven experience owning product positioning, messaging and go-to-market initiatives, including shaping packaging or pricing recommendations, with the ability to explain the commercial reasoning behind your decisions.

  • Hands-on experience bringing products to market with defined targets and measurable outcomes, and a clear understanding of what worked and what didn't.

  • Ability to build and communicate strong commercial value cases or ROI models.

  • A hands-on approach to creating assets such as prototypes, pages and calculators: you build, test and improve rather than simply brief others.

  • Practical experience using AI tools for research and content creation, with an understanding of their strengths and limitations.

  • Confidence working with commercial data, including pipeline, win rates and product attachment, using tools such as HubSpot or Salesforce.

  • Fluent German and English (C1 level).


    • Your salary
  • We offer a salary range of EUR 70,000 – EUR 80,000 per year.
  • Final compensation will be based on experience, skills, and overall fit for the role.

    • Your benefits with us

  • 30 Days Annual Leave with a 5-day workweek: enjoy extra paid time off to rest, recharge, and balance your work and personal life.

  • Flexible Work Model: 100% mobile work within Germany.

  • Fitness & Well-being (choose 1 of 2): stay active your way. Choose either our free Move Republic Program to earn points for rewards, or join EGYM Wellpass for a €20/month co-pay to access a large network of gyms, pools and studios (we cover the rest).

  • Access to Udemy: boost your skills with thousands of high-quality online courses.

  • Deutschland Ticket Subsidy: we cover part of your ticket cost.

  • Company Pension Scheme (bAV): receive an above-average employer contribution in Germany or Austria.

  • Flexible Working Hours: adjust your schedule to fit your lifestyle.

title: Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, EMEA
descriptionHtml:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

GitLab’s Forward Deployed Engineering team is a field-situated product engineering function focused on strategic customer outcomes, artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, and direct contributions to GitLab’s product. This isn't a traditional field engineering, solutions architecture, or professional services role. As a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll work closely with customers while maintaining the technical standards and contribution discipline of a Staff-level product engineer.

You'll work where strategic customer urgency, complex technical ambiguity, and GitLab product execution intersect. You'll partner directly with strategic customers and teams across Product, Engineering, Support, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Solutions Architecture (SA), Customer Success Architecture (CSA), Customer Success Management (CSM), and Professional Services. You'll diagnose and resolve high-impact adoption blockers, contribute production-quality fixes and features, and turn what you learn into repeatable patterns for GitLab and its customers.

Why this role exists

Strategic customers sometimes encounter challenges that are too broad, deep, urgent, or cross-functional for any single team to own from start to finish. These challenges may involve product gaps, performance degradation, scale bottlenecks, AI governance, adoption blockers, architectural constraints, Git usage patterns, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) complexity, application programming interface (API) automation, security requirements, or operational instability.

Forward Deployed Engineering provides technical stewardship in these moments. The team doesn't simply observe, report, or escalate. You'll engage directly, diagnose the underlying technical problem, collaborate with the right teams, contribute code or technical solutions where appropriate, and transition the outcome into normal ownership once the customer is stable and the learning can be reused.

What you’ll do

Product contribution

  • Contribute production-quality code to GitLab’s product and adjacent systems.
  • Develop bug fixes, features, integrations, tooling, and performance improvements when strategic customer outcomes require direct engineering work.
  • Work within GitLab’s product and engineering processes, including issue discovery, merge request creation, testing, review, documentation, and maintainability.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering so customer-driven solutions support long-term product direction rather than becoming one-off customizations.
  • Turn blockers discovered in the field into durable product improvements, reference architectures, documentation, and repeatable implementation patterns.

Strategic technical stewardship

  • Engage with strategically important customers when adoption, retention, executive confidence, or public trust is materially at risk.
  • Diagnose complex problems across GitLab product behavior, customer architecture, Git internals, CI/CD workflows, API usage, observability, infrastructure, networking, and cloud environments.
  • Coordinate across Product, Engineering, SRE, Support, SA, CSA, CSM, Professional Services, and customer technical teams to drive resolution from discovery through handoff.
  • Provide recommendations grounded in data, traces, and systems analysis to improve GitLab usage, workflows, automation, and architecture.
  • Create durable outcomes without establishing permanent dependency on Forward Deployed Engineering.

AI adoption and agentic software development lifecycle

  • Drive governed, measurable, and production-oriented adoption of GitLab Duo Agent Platform with strategic customers.
  • Identify and resolve AI adoption blockers involving governance, usage controls, auditability, security, compliance, operating models, workflow design, and integrations.
  • Develop customer-safe adoption patterns for the agentic software development lifecycle (SDLC), AI-assisted development, intent-based review, AI governance, and human-in-the-loop software delivery.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Field, and Customer Success teams to turn AI adoption learning into reusable guidance and product improvements.

Thought leadership

  • Create technical narratives grounded in customer experience and product reality that can help shape the industry’s approach.
  • Contribute to Well-Architected Frameworks, whitepapers, webinars, reference architectures, technical strategy memos, and adoption frameworks.
  • Guide ideas through discovery, formulation, validation, amplification, and adoption across GitLab.
  • Partner with SA, CSA, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Product Marketing Management, CSM, Support, and executive stakeholders to make technical thought leadership a shared company capability.

What you’ll bring

  • Staff-level experience building, operating, or improving complex production software systems.
  • Experience contributing to large, mature product codebases with high standards for testing, maintainability, performance, and security.
  • Strong Ruby on Rails or Go experience and the ability to contribute directly to GitLab’s product and adjacent systems.
  • Experience with AI-assisted software development, agentic workflows, AI governance, model evaluation, context management, prompt and workflow design, or AI adoption in enterprise environments.
  • Experience diagnosing complex system behavior across application code, data stores, infrastructure, observability, networking, APIs, and customer usage patterns.
  • Deep knowledge of modern DevSecOps workflows, including Git, merge requests, CI/CD, security controls, compliance needs, and enterprise software delivery.
  • Experience working with strategic customers or senior technical stakeholders in ambiguous, high-impact situations.
  • The ability to coordinate across product, engineering, field, and customer teams without formal authority.
  • Strong written communication and sound judgment, including the ability to create technical narratives and distinguish reusable product work from customer-specific customization.

Strongly preferred qualifications

  • Direct experience with GitLab as a platform, including GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, or GitLab Self-Managed.
  • Production experience with Ruby on Rails, Go, PostgreSQL, Redis, Sidekiq, Vue, TypeScript, Kubernetes, Docker, Linux, or observability tools.
  • Deep familiarity with Git internals, repository performance, large-scale Git usage patterns, or GitLab Runner behavior.
  • Experience creating technical thought-leadership materials, such as whitepapers, technical talks, architecture frameworks, requests for comments, public technical writing, or internal strategy documents.
  • A background in performance engineering, site reliability engineering, platform engineering, infrastructure engineering, or distributed systems.
  • Experience working in open source or highly asynchronous engineering environments.

Technologies and domains

Directly relevant technologies and domains include:

  • Ruby on Rails
  • Go
  • AI-assisted development and the agentic SDLC
  • PostgreSQL
  • Redis and Sidekiq
  • Git internals
  • GitLab CI/CD and Runner architecture
  • Kubernetes and containers
  • Terraform
  • Linux, networking, observability, and performance analysis
  • Vue and TypeScript
  • APIs and automation
  • DevSecOps governance, security, and compliance

What this role is not

This role isn't:

  • A generic field engineering role.
  • A proof-of-concept factory.
  • A replacement for Solutions Architecture, Customer Success Architecture, Customer Success Management, Professional Services, Support, SRE, Product, or Engineering.
  • A customer-specific customization function.
  • Unbilled Professional Services.
  • A requirements-gathering role that only escalates to Product.
  • An AI evangelism role disconnected from product execution.

Success measures

Success in this role may include:

  • Stabilizing strategic customer adoption or retention risks.
  • Fixing product bugs or contributing features.
  • Removing AI adoption blockers for strategic accounts.
  • Creating reusable implementation patterns and transitioning them to long-term owners.
  • Producing or enabling Well-Architected Frameworks, whitepapers, webinars, or technical narratives.
  • Resolving cross-functional customer challenges without creating permanent dependency on Forward Deployed Engineering.
  • Equipping Product, Engineering, Support, CSA, CSM, Professional Services, and SA teams with better guidance based on learning from the field.
  • Increasing adoption and effective use of GitLab capabilities, especially GitLab Duo and GitLab Duo Agent Platform, in targeted accounts.

About the team

The Forward Deployed Engineering team connects strategic customer needs with GitLab product execution. The team works directly with customers and across GitLab to resolve complex adoption challenges, contribute durable product improvements, and create reusable technical guidance. Its goal is to stabilize urgent situations, improve the product, and transition ongoing ownership to the appropriate team rather than create a permanent dependency.

Ideal candidate profile

You're a Staff-level product or platform engineer who can operate in the field without becoming field-only. You're comfortable reading traces, writing production code, debugging architecture, discussing AI governance, leading a customer technical session, opening a merge request, outlining a whitepaper, and coordinating across teams to achieve a strategic customer outcome.

You're not simply a strong communicator with technical awareness. You're a credible engineer with the judgment, presence, and narrative ability to turn customer reality into product contributions, adoption guidance, and company-level thought leadership.

We welcome candidates with different backgrounds and levels of experience. Many successful candidates don't meet every qualification. If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply and let our recruiting team assess your application.

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

  • Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
  • Flexible Paid Time Off 
  • Team Member Resource Groups
  • Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Growth and Development Fund
  • Parental Leave 

Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.

Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.
